    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that incorporating secret ingredients into your burger patties elevates the dish in unexpected ways. Some components flavor the meat while others enhance the texture. For an add-in that does both — with a delicious underlying creaminess — look no further than yogurt. The dairy works as a ground beef tenderizer, making a burger that's softer and full of moisture. Not to mention, yogurt is an effective enhancement in chicken or turkey patties, too.

    Yogurt's contained lactic acid functions as a mild, but nevertheless efficient, tenderizer, lightly marinating the meat. The inclusion of a liquid naturally adds lots of moisture to a burger — you certainly won't have to worry about a disappointingly dry result. Plus, the ingredient lends the burger a lightly creamy mouthfeel.

    And if you use Greek yogurt for the task, you'll get a nice dose of added protein, too. Mix in a quarter cup of whole milk Greek yogurt — a quantity suitable for a pound of meat — and you'll up the dish by 5.5 grams of protein. This yogurt's extra fat content will further prevent dryness, all while forming a patty that's not too loose, making a burger rendition that stands out.

    It has been revealed that working yogurt into your beef patties doesn't require any special technique. You can simply stir the dairy with the beef in a bowl, seasoning with salt and pepper in parallel. Follow by forming the patties as usual, then lightly brush the exterior with oil to prevent unwanted adhesion. Prepare the yogurt burgers using your preferred method, whether you're fond of using a skillet or grilling burgers like a pro. However, if you notice your mixture appears too wet, consider adding a binder — chia seeds are a fantastic option to absorb moisture but keep things tender and juicy; panko breadcrumbs will also absorb excess liquid while keeping the bite of each burger soft.

    Sources indicate that such a burger tastes delicious with classic seasonings, but don't rule out creative modifications, too. The pairing of yogurt and beef recalls Greek and Middle Eastern cuisine, so consider integrating Eastern Mediterranean seasonings into the build.

    In a recent development, A Greek burger spin could fold in oregano, lemon, and feta — core flavors of a Greek salad. A kofta-style patty might up the spice, working in earthy cumin, a dash of spicy harissa, and grated garlic into the mix. Alternatively, season the meat in a sweet direction by using simply turmeric and onions; the ingredients will set you up for a wide array of flavorful condiments. Build out the meal with an aromatic herbal yogurt sauce, a bold dose of roasted peppers, or a marinated arugula salad, and you'll make a burger rendition that'll become a frequent part of the rotation.

You use an app, tap a feature, and wonder how it was built. Maybe it is a fast search bar, a clever clipboard trick, or a mechanic in an old game. Until recently, finding out meant months of learning disassemblers and reading assembly code. A latest open-source project called REA changes that. It has earned more than 430,000 stars on GitHub, and in this guide I will explain what it does, which problems it solves, and how you can start using it today. In this guide The problem with reverse engineering How REA solves it How REA works What REA can analyze Real examples How to get started REA at a glance Using REA responsibly Frequently asked questions The Problem: Reverse Engineering Is Hard Reverse engineering is the practice of studying finished software to understand how it works. It is powerful, but it has never been beginner-friendly. If you have tried it, or even thought about trying it, you have probably run into these obstacles. 1. A steep learning curve Reading assembly code and pseudocode takes a long time to learn. Many curious developers give up before they get their first useful result. 2. Too many tools and no single workflow An Electron app needs one approach. An Android APK needs another. A .NET assembly, a native binary, and a website each have their own tools, file formats, and tricks. 3. Slow, manual investigation Even experts can spend hours following one function through strings, calls, and references just to understand a single small feature. 4. AI answers you cannot verify If you ask a general chatbot how an app works, it may give a confident answer that is simply invented. Without evidence, you cannot tell what is real. 5. Painful setup Connecting analysis tools to an AI agent usually requires custom scripts and configuration, and it is easy to break. The Solution: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) REA is a free, MIT-licensed project that connects your AI agent to professional reverse engineering tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol). MCP is a standard way for AI agents to use external tools. In simple terms, REA acts as a bridge between your agent and the software you want to understand. Here is how it answers each problem above. The Problem How REA Solves It Steep learning curve You ask in plain English. Your agent runs the tools and explains the results. Too many tools One MCP server covers native binaries, Electron apps, Android, .NET, websites, and dozens of other formats. Slow and manual The agent traces code, references, and calls for you. Answers you cannot verify Every result includes the evidence and limitations behind it. Painful setup One command registers REA with your agent and backs up your existing configuration. You do not need the app’s source code. You point your agent at the app, ask a question, and REA helps it trace the answer. How REA Works You ask a question. For example, how a feature in a particular app works. The agent calls REA. It uses MCP to inspect the target and trace the relevant code. REA returns findings. These include code, references, and clearly marked unknowns. The agent acts on them. It can explain the behavior, ask follow-up questions, or write and test its own version of the feature. The same workflows are available from the terminal, so you can also script them without an agent. Analysis runs locally on your machine. Your agent receives the tool results, and your AI provider’s own data policy applies to that part. What Can REA Analyze? The range of supported targets is one of REA’s biggest strengths. These are the main groups. Native programs and binaries REA returns pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls, and references. Deep native analysis uses an engine you already have, such as Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, or Kuna. It also supports GNU objdump and Rizin for offline inspection. JavaScript and Electron apps This is the easiest place to start, because static JavaScript analysis needs no native engine. REA recovers modules, imports, source maps, routes, IPC connections, and native add-on relationships. Android apps and devices REA can inspect APK manifests, classes, decompiled methods, signatures, and resources. Through adb, it can also look at packages, processes, and logs on an emulator or a real phone. Flutter apps and JEB projects are supported too. .NET and managed code For .NET assemblies, REA reads metadata, CIL instructions, and native dependencies without running the program. Websites and network captures REA can inspect page structure, scripts, and network activity using a Chrome-family browser. It can also read saved HAR and Fiddler SAZ files to examine requests, responses, and exposed payloads. Specialist formats The list continues with Go and Rust binaries, GPU code objects, GGUF and safetensors model files, Unity IL2CPP metadata, Godot PCK archives, PE imports and certificates, ELF notes, Linux kernel modules, WebAssembly, EVM bytecode, SQLite databases, firmware images, packet captures, and PyInstaller executables. Most of these use built-in static inspection, so no extra software is required. Real Examples: What Has REA Done? The project publishes several case studies on its website. DX-Ball sound panning. REA followed a sound call into a helper function and turned incomplete pseudocode into C. The reconstruction passed 3,205 test cases against the original x86 code and matched all 63 compiled function bytes. Notion’s clipboard bridge. REA traced how Notion’s Electron app moves clipboard data from the renderer through preload and IPC into the main process, including the rich clipboard format. TH04 bullet patterns. REA recovered the angle calculations of a classic DOS game and compared the rebuilt C++ with the original compiler output. Bonus: build RL environments from a web app REA can record a web app session and turn its API calls into tools an AI agent can use. It then exports a runnable environment for reinforcement learning or for testing how well an agent completes tasks. With a saved HAR file, the command looks like this: rea environment-build ./session.har ./my-env --name my-env --json You then run the result with AgentEnv and Docker, and add your own tasks and reward checks. How to Get Started With REA You need Node.js and npm. The project lists supported Node versions as 22.x (22.23.4 or newer), 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), or 26.12.1 and above. Step 1: Run the setup command npx rea-agents setup Step 2: Choose your agents and approve the changes Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents. It demonstrates you the proposed changes first and keeps backups of your existing configuration. Step 3: Restart your agent The new MCP server is loaded when the agent starts again. Step 4: Ask your first question Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. Prefer the terminal? You can inspect an extracted Electron app or ASAR file directly: npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json To keep REA installed, run npm install --global rea-agents. REA changes rapidly, so use rea update to stay current. Updating is also the first fix to try if you run into a bug. REA at a Glance What makes it special REA combines the reach of dozens of analysis tools with the convenience of an AI agent. It helps you understand software you do not have source code for, and it backs each conclusion with evidence instead of guesses. The range of supported formats, from native binaries to Electron apps to Android devices, is unusually broad for a free tool. Key features Works through MCP with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, and other agents Evidence and limitations attached to every result Local analysis on your own machine A full command-line interface for scripting Support for dozens of file and app types An RL environment builder Guides and case studies on the official website Pricing REA itself: free and open source (MIT license) Commercial engines such as IDA Pro, Hopper, and JEB: you must obtain these legally under their own licenses Ghidra: a free option for native analysis; see the setup guide for details Perfect for Developers, security researchers, students, software preservationists, and anyone who wants to understand how an app works. Using REA Responsibly Use REA only on software you own or are authorized to examine. The project is intended for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you have permission to study. It does not permit cracked tools, stolen license keys, or bypassing license restrictions. Read the project’s disclaimer before you start. Also be careful where you download it from. The project warns that a similar repository name or a copied README does not make a download official. Use only these sources: GitHub: github.com/morluto/rea Website: rea.tools npm package: rea-agents Frequently Asked Questions Do I need Hopper or Ghidra? Only for deep native binary analysis. JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native engine, and setup can install Hopper with your approval. Does REA upload my app? No. Analysis runs locally. Your agent sees the results, and its provider has its own data policy. Which AI agents work with REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers can use it. What should I do if I find a bug? Update first, because a recent release may already include the fix. If the problem continues, open an problem on GitHub with your REA version, the target type, the steps to reproduce, and the error output. Final Thoughts The old problem was simple: understanding software without source code took too much skill, too many tools, and too much time. REA’s answer is just as simple. It gives your AI agent the tools to investigate, and it requires the agent to show its evidence. Whether you want to learn how a favorite feature works, study a classic game, or inspect an Electron app, REA is a strong place to start. Just make sure you use it only on software you are allowed to examine.

    Give Canned Baked Beans A Delicious Upgrade With A Drizzle Of This Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Honey)

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When you need a side to go along with your main dinner entree and you need one fast, it's reassuring to know that shelf-stable, pantry-sitting canned goods have got your back. Included in Food Republic's list of inexpensive canned foods you'll use all the time are beans, and along with the plain black or red varieties (which typically need to be combined with other ingredients to make a reasonable side), you could also reach for scrumptious, creamy baked beans. But while they're totally fine heated up straight from the can, they can certainly benefit from a drizzle of molasses.

    Industry observers note that molasses might not be the first thing you think of when you consider add-ins, but many homemade recipes call for it, and for good reason. Made by boiling down sugarcane juice or refining sugar, the rich, thick syrup is slightly smoky and sweet, with robust, burnt caramel notes, making it a perfect match for deepening the flavor of sometimes weak-tasting canned baked beans and bringing them closer to homemade.

    Sources indicate that it is for this reason that molasses is also preferable to honey here. Honey is intensely sweet, can taste almost floral at times, and has a delicate flavor, whereas molasses is bolder and has a meatier taste that can make its presence known among the other ingredients in the dish.

    It's important to note that there are three main types of molasses: light, dark, and blackstrap, and they each have different flavor profiles. For canned baked beans, you'll likely want to stick with light or dark because blackstrap is intensely bitter (also, light is the sweetest of the three, so if sweetness is important to you, go with that one). If you're heating the beans on the stove, you can start by drizzling in about half a tablespoon of molasses per 28-ounce can, bringing the mixture to a boil, and then simmering for about 10 minutes. If you're baking them, likewise, just stir in the molasses before putting the dish in the oven — it couldn't be simpler.

    If you don't have any molasses sitting about, don't panic. There are plenty of other additions that can help upgrade canned baked beans and make them taste less, well, pantry-fied. Take brown sugar, for example — did you know that it's often just white sugar and molasses combined? A little bit will still bring that sweet contrast to balance out the savory flavors and give you a deeper, more complex finish.

    Another great option is one you might normally use on your pancakes: maple syrup. You don't want to use the fake stuff that's primarily made of corn syrup and artificial flavors and colors, but rather 100% real Grade A maple syrup for the best flavor. Its sweetness again deliciously contrasts with and enhances the canned baked beans' savoriness, while the maple flavor adds its unique caramelly, toffee-like notes to the dish.

    Make Your Next Breakfast Sandwich Korean-Style For A Major Fiber & Flavor Boost

    • Think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind.
    • Industry observers note that easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind. However, bread-based dishes are widely enjoyed in the East Asian country, both in cafes and as street food. An especially popular breakfast rendition is gilgeori toast, a comforting breakfast sandwich stuffed with eggs and shredded vegetables.

    Industry observers note that easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation. Traditionally, this sandwich calls for a fluffy loaf of milk or brioche bread, the buttery soft texture turning crisp on the outside once toasted. Meanwhile, the filling comprises a variable shredded vegetable medley: Cabbage traditionally forms the centerpiece, joined by carrots, onions, scallions, and often garlic chives. Mixed with egg and then pan-fried into an aesthetic golden-brown patty, the filling delectably complements the soft bread. Gilgeori is usually rounded out with a sprinkle of sugar and a drizzle of ketchup and mustard.

    It's an assembly that easily comes together during bleary morning hours, yet nevertheless offers a nutritious start to the day. One sandwich can pack in around six ounces of shredded cabbage, which amounts to over 4 grams of fiber. Add up the fiber from a tablespoon of carrot, two of sliced onion, and two whole green onions, and you're including another 1.5 grams. Then, add in two slices of thick-cut brioche sandwich bread, and you've got an extra 2. That's about 7.5 grams, which is around a quarter of what you need a day, already knocked out by breakfast. Mixed with the roughly 6.5 grams of protein from the egg alongside filling bread, the sandwich serves as a terrific way to start the day.

    Industry observers note that the morning isn't always the best time to precisely reconstruct a recipe. Thankfully, gilgeori toast welcomes a wide array of reinterpretations and ingredients. Starting with the bread, feel free to swap the milk bread for sourdough, whole wheat, or even a convenient store-bought whole grain like Ezekiel or Dave's Killer. You'll lose out on some of the dish's airiness, but potentially gain extra fiber content in the process. Two slices of Dave's Killer 21 Whole Grains and Seeds contain some 8 grams of fiber, more than doubling the total of the sandwich.

    Up the satiation further by adding on a slice of seared ham, a filling also enjoyed in Korea. And cheese is always welcome, whether American, cheddar, or fontina – Martha Stewart's go-to for breakfast sandwiches. Instead of the sugar sprinkle, lend the dish a sweet note by using jam: Raspberry or cherry jam makes a great fit. Not to mention, you can replace the ketchup and mustard with a condiment of your preference; you can buy a bottle of Gochujang Sriracha Hot Sauce online, for instance. The template of bread and shredded vegetables works with many flavors, perfect for morning enjoyment.

    According to recent reports, warm spices on French toast create a cozy, aromatic breakfast dish that warms your sinuses as much as your tongue. While traditional cinnamon is always a solid choice, cardamom French toast adds new layers of fresh, almost herbal notes for something far more complex and just as compatible with your other favorite seasonings.

    Some folks call cardamom the queen of spices — and for good reason. As flavorful as it is versatile, it's a shelf-stable ingredient that lasts a long time, grinds easily into a powder, and seems to taste amazing with just about any sweet recipe you could think of. While it can be a tad on the expensive side, small amounts suffuse your French toast with deep flavor, so even a small jar of seeds can last you quite a while. The key is to mix it with your other dried spices to create a delicate flavor profile similar to mulled drinks, festive winter desserts, and spiced ciders.

    Industry observers note that six pods should yield about half a teaspoon of ground spice, enough for roughly six pieces of French toast (though pod sizes vary). Since you want a smooth batter without much texture, it's best to grind the seeds into a fine powder before mixing. The moisture from eggs and milk should help protect the delicate spice, but remember that heat affects the flavor release of spices. Gently toasting the pods beforehand is a great way to bump up the flavor without using more of the pricey ingredient.

    In a recent development, though cardamom has quite a bit of flavor, it's also rather delicate and can slip into the background or be the star of the show, depending on your preferences. In sweet dishes, there are few warm spices it pairs poorly with, and more obscure ingredients can really elevate its flavor for something showstopping.

    Recent findings suggest that just about any warming spice you'd associate with the colder months should pair beautifully with cardamom. Cinnamon is a bold counterpart that can carry most of the flavor profile without overshadowing it when used in moderation. Allspice and cloves are a match made in heaven, providing an almost berry-like warmth to counteract cardamom's cool, herbal notes. Ground or fresh ginger can add a touch of sharpness that offers quite a bit of contrast, providing a similar bite on the tongue to garlic that's far more compatible with sugary bases.

    Sources indicate that if you really want to bump up the flavor of cardamom, don't stick to just spices. Floral notes from things like dried and ground orange peels, lychee, or guava really round out your French toast without overpowering your spices. These are highly compatible with cardamom and make your breakfast taste almost like a pomander, with an incredible bouquet of aromas the second your bread hits the pan. You can also use food-safe flavoring oils instead, mixing them into your wet ingredients for greater control over how much flavor you're adding.

    #115084. The Absolute Best Pizza In Your State

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4127 w)

    The Absolute Best Pizza In Your State

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that there's probably no food more universally adored among Americans than pizza.
    • This list sets aside nationwide pizza chains and restaurants that happen to have pizza on the menu, and seeks to highlight the most delicious pizza in each state.
    • A well-traveled mainstay of Huntsville, Alabama, Valentina's Pizzeria has a reputation for serving New York-style pizza in a deep Southern atmosphere alongside other confections and dishes made in an Italian-American tradition.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that there's probably no food more universally adored among Americans than pizza. Aside from being extremely customizable, every state has its own version of the best pizza — at least 15 distinct varieties and styles of making pizza can be found in the U.S. This makes it difficult to compare them. After all, the differences between a Detroit deep-dish and a chewy New Haven pie are many.

    This list sets aside nationwide pizza chains and restaurants that happen to have pizza on the menu, and seeks to highlight the most delicious pizza in each state. We considered customer reviews from all over the internet, as well as any regional or national honors attributed to each pizza, and compared the overall cultural legacy and impact of each restaurant. What we ended up with was delicious pizza places that were worthy of being the best in each state. When a good frozen pizza (or even the best frozen pizzas) won't cut it, these are the spots to check out.

    A well-traveled mainstay of Huntsville, Alabama, Valentina's Pizzeria has a reputation for serving New York-style pizza in a deep Southern atmosphere alongside other confections and dishes made in an Italian-American tradition. Joe Carlucci, the maestro behind Valentina's Pizzeria, is a co-founder of the World Pizza Champions organization, and his pizzeria is a local favorite — just check the comments on any of Valentina's Pizzeria's posts.

    25783 Huntsville Brownsferry Rd, Madison, AL 35756.

    Recent findings suggest that people love Moose's Tooth Pub & Pizzeria because it delivers on its goal of offering a "gourmet pizza experience, focusing on creative, quality food in a casual environment." The menu (with a robust list of temporary featured pizzas) reflects a creative urge to innovate. Moose's Tooth is the best-reviewed pizza in Alaska, according to Yelp and Google. There's no shortage of outdoor ambience in Alaska, so in addition to its indoor pub seating, Moose's Tooth offers outdoor, fireside seating for crisp days and nights.

    3300 Old Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK 99503.

    Every pie at Via Della Slice Shop is crafted with artful attention to detail, and it's this skill and the friendly customer service that keep people coming back for more. Though a small and relatively simple operation, the restaurant is dedicated to making pizza of the highest quality; it proofs its dough for at least two days. According to Yelp, the vodka pizza is a particular favorite among returning customers, but Via Della is noted for its rotating flavors.

    222 N 5th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

    While DeLuca's Pizza has recently received accolades for its unconventional Spite Burger, it is best known for its brick-oven-baked pizza pies sold out of two locations in Hot Springs, Arkansas. Pizza influencer Dave Portnoy gave DeLuca's pizza an 8.7 out of 10, adding that it "blew [his] socks off [and] can compete with anybody in the country." And the non-influencers love it, too, with some people even driving multiple hours just to get a bite.

    It has been revealed that tony's Pizza Napoletana was recognized this year as the No. 5 best pizzeria in the world, according to 50 Top Pizza. Tony's is just as popular with customers as with critics, as it's maintained a high star rating through tens of thousands of eviews on Google. Tony Gemigani — owner and 13-time World Pizza Champion — has spent years perfecting his pies; any West Coast pizza crawl would be incomplete without a visit to Tony's.

    1570 Stockton St, San Francisco, CA 94133.

    Recent findings suggest that blue Pan Pizza offers delicious, Detroit-style pizza with a little bit of Denver flair. It's known for its Detroit-style pies, but it offers other versions and has been noted by folks for its tasty gluten-free options as well.

    Detroit-style pizza is pan-baked pizza, and Blue Pan even serves to-go pies in rectangular, bright blue boxes made to look like its titular bakeware. Blue Pan was voted Readers' Choice for Best Denver Pizzeria by Denver Westword in 2024 and enjoys a huge local following.

    A staple of Connecticut and specifically New Haven-style pizza since 1938, Sally's Apizza is a legendary spot amongst locals and pizza fanatics. New Haven-style pizza is made of high-hydration dough and cooked at a high heat in order to achieve a chewy, airy crust.

    A new fan of Sally's wrote on Yelp, "It was a perfect meal, in a nice, cozy old school spot, that I'll definitely be craving until I'm back in town.".

    237 Wooster St, New Haven, CT 06511.

    La Pizzeria Metro is a lovely little pizza place with two Delaware locations that offer a breezy, friendly dining experience and delicious pizza. Customers can even settle at the bar and tables with a view of pizza chefs at work.

    According to recent reports, la Pizzeria Metro's many specialty pizzas are named after landmark spots in Wilmington, an apt choice given how popular the place is with locals. One local reviewer wrote, "La Pizzeria Metro absolutely nails [creative pizza]. Their pizzas somehow manage to feel both authentic and wildly inventive.".

    Sources indicate that it's no secret online that Florida's pizza options leave much to be desired. But Satchel's Pizza in Gainesville is a diamond in the rough.

    It's a beloved destination for locals who praise both its delicious pizza and eclectic atmosphere. Some would even argue it's not just the best pizza in Florida; it might just be the best in the south. Even with thousands of reviews online, Satchel's maintains a very high star average rating.

    1800 NE 23rd Ave, Gainesville, FL 32609.

    Sources indicate that antico Pizza Napoletana is a pizzeria located in Atlanta's Little Italia. Founded by Giovanni "Gio" Di Palma, Antico offers only Neapolitan-style pizza cooked in wood-burning ovens, and thanks to its impeccable quality, earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2023. The pizza is so good, in fact, that it earned the highest score out of all pizzerias reviewed in Zagat's first survey of pizza places in major U.S. cities.

    Sources indicate that though Pizza Mamo only began selling pies in 2020, it's quickly been established as a neighborhood mainstay in Honolulu and has earned an Ilima Award — Hawaii's most prestigious restaurant recognition. Pizza Mamo's pies are based on a four-day fermented dough that provides a satisfying, chewy consistency in every slice. A local Yelp reviewer wrote, "Best pizza I've had on the island ... the pepperoni has a nice spice to it, and the dough is PERFECT.".

    16 N Hotel St, Honolulu, HI 96817.

    Recent findings suggest that despite its remote location, Embers by the Lake has garnered tons of glowing online reviews – and the pizzeria's gorgeous lakeside backdrop is only a small part of what customers love. A great spot for family outings, Embers by the Lake has earned official recognition determined by customers, entities, and critics, including a local organization called North Idaho Life, which awarded it the first 5-Star Dining Destination Award.

    12008 N Woodland Beach Dr, Hauser, ID 83854.

    Industry observers note that vito and Nick's Pizzeria is known for its Chicago tavern-style pies, which are made with a round, cracker-thin crust and cut into squares. It's a parlor that's been in business for more than 75 years and is an iconic institution to locals and tourists alike. The CBS Chicago Pizza Tournament awarded Vito and Nick's the grand prize in 2023, and the parlor has been positively featured on Food Network's "Diners, Drive-ins and Dives.".

    In a recent development, tre Mori is much more than a pizza restaurant — the menu offers finely crafted pasta dishes and baked breads — but the pizza is definitely its signature. Dedicated to an old-style Italian sensibility, Tre Mori utilizes fresh and home-prepared ingredients, as well as supplies and foods imported from Italy (including the beautiful brick oven). On Yelp, Tre Mori is a top-100 US pizza joint, and on Onebite, it earns consistently positive reviews from customers.

    8220 E 106th St Suite 200, Indianapolis, IN 46256.

    Fong's Pizza in Des Moines occupies the same space that once housed the oldest Chinese restaurant in America. As such, it offers a fusion of Chinese flavors and Italian fundamentals. Fong's claims to be the originator of the crab rangoon pizza (Alton Brown swears by it), and the restaurant earns great customer feedback for its fresh ingredients and timely service.

    317 E Court Ave, Des Moines, IA 50309.

    Recent findings suggest that even though Back Alley Pizza has only been operating for a little over 10 years, it has become a staple of Newton, Kansas, and a magnet for regional recognition. On Yelp, satisfied customers rejoice over the best pizza they've ever had, period. Though Back Alley Pizza doesn't claim a signature "style" of pizza, it does tout its original BBQ pizza as a signature. But you'll be happy with any slice you try.

    Miguel's Pizza feels like a well-loved small business with a dedicated following and a commitment to capturing Kentucky's rustic charm in combination with a warm, friendly atmosphere. Pizza Today has featured Miguel's as a must-stop destination, and many recognize the pizzeria as a key element in the economic development of Kentucky's Red River Gorge. All of that is because of the quality of the pizza, which people just can't get enough of.

    1890 Natural Bridge Rd, Slade, KY 40376.

    Sources indicate that zander White, founder of Zee's Pizzeria, pursued pizza-making as a hobby until the COVID-19 pandemic, during which he had to find a upcoming way to support his family. White was so successful selling pies from his kitchen that he opened Zee's Pizzeria, which was named one of the top pizza places in New Orleans by Gambit Weekly. Customers appreciate the thin crust, sweet sauce, and classic taste.

    3914 Baronne St, Fresh Orleans, LA 70115.

    The purveyors at Brickyard Hollow Brewing Firm (which began in Yarmouth) realized that few things pair better with a glass of craft beer than a slice of craft pizza, which has become as much of a draw as the beer – if not more so.

    In a recent development, brickyard Hollow has a greater mission to provide fun and comfort to local Maine communities and residents looking to connect more closely with their neighbors. It's received rave reviews from local critics and is rapidly expanding thanks to overwhelming regional support.

    It has been revealed that in December 2024, Barstool pizza reviewer Dave Portnoy stopped by TinyBrickOven to do a quick slice review. He gave TinyBrickOven's pizza a 7.9/10 rating and $60,000 to turn the small business significant. It was that good. TinyBrickOven is a staple of Baltimore, with local customers and other supporters even accepting the owner's self-anointed title, "the Michael Jordan of pizza.".

    1036 Light St, Baltimore, MD 21230.

    Widely regarded as Boston's oldest operating pizza place, Regina Pizzeria has been serving slices and pies around Boston's North End since 1926. The quality comes from an impeccable dough — chewy yet crisp and perfectly charred — that's baked inside a 900-degree gas-fired oven. Boston Magazine calls it one of the city's best, and in 2018, Tripadvisor named Regina Pizzeria the best in the nation. Taste of Massachusetts included it in its list of top 11 favorite pizzas in the state.

    In 2024, Yelp named Loui's Pizza in Hazel Park, Michigan, as the best pizza spot in the Midwest. It's been family-owned since 1977, and for nearly half a century, it's been pumping out top-tier Detroit-style pies that are chewy, crisp, cheesy, and properly sauced. The Detroit Metro Times ranked Loui's as the No. 1 Detroit-style pizza in the area, citing its "tangy sauce, crispy caramelized edges, and an abundance of cheese" as a few of the reasons why this pizza stands out.

    23141 Dequindre Rd, Hazel Park, MI 48030.

    Sources indicate that when you have the endorsement from global food aficionado Andrew Zimmern, you know you're doing something right. Punch Pizza is the people's pizzeria, a beloved St. Paul institution that has now expanded to 12 locations. It specializes in Neapolitan-style pizza, cooked for about a minute and a half in a scorching-hot, wood-burning oven. It has earned numerous awards and recognitions, including a Quality Business Award in 2025.

    In a recent development, leña Pizza + Bagels is giving Mississippi some long-deserved culinary attention. Chef and owner Marisol Doyle grew up in Mexico, moved to Mississippi, and studied pizza making in Naples, Italy. The restaurant was rapidly named one of the best in the United States by both the Fresh York Times and the prestigious Italian pizza review board, 50 Top Pizza. However, the biggest honor came in 2024, when Doyle was named one of the top 100 pizza chefs in the world.

    331 Cotton Row, Cleveland, MS 38732.

    Recent findings suggest that you've heard of Latest York-, New Haven-, and Detroit-style pizza, but — unless you're from Missouri, you probably aren't familiar with St. Louis-style pies. And Pirrone's Pizzeria, which has been around since 1976, arguably makes the best one in the state. The rectangular dough is crisp and cracker-thin and covered in melted Provel, a triple-blend processed cheese invented in St. Louis.

    1775 Washington St, Florissant, MO 63033.

    Eugene's Pizza has remained a community staple for over 60 years. In 2015 and 2016, it was the back-to-back champion of the Montana Mint pizza bracket, and in 2026, Reader's Digest recognized the pizzeria as the best in Montana. Eugene's serves some wild pies, with topping options ranging from taco-seasoned ground beef and sauerkraut to shrimp and mandarin oranges.

    193 Klein Ave, Glasgow, MT 59230.

    Industry observers note that founded in 1919 by World War I veteran Alfonso Orsi, the bakery and pizzeria has racked up thousands of excellent reviews on Google. Its near-perfect score has a lot to do with its pizza dough — prepared fresh in small batches every morning using a simple recipe of yeast, salt, water, and high-gluten wheat flour. Tripadvisor ranks it the top pizzeria in Omaha, and our sister site, Mashed, listed it as the best Italian restaurant in Nebraska.

    621 Pacific St, Omaha, NE 68108.

    According to recent reports, red Dwarf is a triumvirate of pleasures: it's a pizzeria, rum-infused Tiki party, and rock show all in one. The Detroit-style pies have a "crispy edge [and an] airy center" and are loaded with topping combinations that include everything from brown sugar-glazed ham, pineapple, and jalapeño to mushrooms, peppers, and garlic creme sauce. In 2025, Red Dwarf won the Reader's Choice Best Pizza Award from Las Vegas Weekly, and commenters on Facebook, Reddit, and Google agree it's the best pizza in town.

    1305 Vegas Valley Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89169.

    It has been revealed that in New England, New Haven-style pizza gets all the attention, but venture a few hundred miles north, and you'll find another popular regional variety: Greek-style. With these pies, the dough bakes in a high-walled pan that's generously coated with olive oil to achieve an extra-crisp, almost fried bottom crust. And few places execute it better than New Hampshire's Tilton House of Pizza. It appears on roundups as the best pizza place in New Hampshire and has a near-perfect rating on Google.

    In a recent development, new Jersey certainly takes its pizza seriously. Part of that reputation can be attributed to the De Lorenzo family, who opened their first New Jersey restaurant in 1936. In 2021, Food and Wine recognized New Jersey as the best state for pizza in the country, calling out De Lorenzo's specifically as "one of the finest classic pies in the entire Northeast." Its namesake tomato pie is hand-stretched, layered with cheese — then sauce — and baked until charred.

    According to the Albuquerque Journal, Pizza Barn is slinging some of the best pies in all of Fresh Mexico. And any pizzeria with a fireplace and a drive-thru deserves special recognition. Pizza Barn is known for its roasted green chiles — a popular condiment throughout the state — which it liberally scatters over its pies and breadsticks.

    11 Plaza Loop, Edgewood, NM 87015.

    According to recent reports, john's of Bleecker, the famed no-slice pizzeria, has been blazing dough in its coal-fired oven since 1929. The pies are thin, crisp, and beautifully blistered, topped with a just-sweet-enough tomato sauce, and then baked fast and hot. With Google reviewers praising its old-school traditions, service, and the pizza itself, this is one of the most respected Fresh York City pizzerias — if not the world.

    278 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014.

    Recent findings suggest that oakwood Pizza Box anchors the pizza scene in the North Carolina Research Triangle. It was awarded Best Pizza in 2026 by Midtown Magazine, a publication that highlights life in the greater Raleigh area. It serves an excellent Northeastern-style pizza: thin, foldable, cheesy, and not overly sauced. Its square pies are about the size of a large pillowcase and can be ordered with a sesame seed crust.

    In a recent development, north Dakota has carved out its own style of pizza, which is heartier than your average Neapolitan pie or Latest York-style slice. Since the early 2000s, Rhombus Guys have been baking doughy, tire-sized pizzas that have earned it the reputation as one of the best (and most inventive) pizzerias in the state. The restaurant's signature T-Rex pizza — a hulking combination of pepperoni, sausage, and other toppings — won the Grand Forks People's Choice competition six years in a row.

    Rarely do you see such a consensus on Reddit and Facebook, but when it comes to Il Rione, almost everyone agrees that it makes one of the best pies in Cleveland — if not the state. It serves a gorgeous Newly introduced York-style pizza that, in 2025, beat out 32 other pizzerias to win the title of Best Pizza in the Land from the local media outlet I'm From Cleveland. It's also a favorite of Iron Chef (and Cleveland native) Michael Symon.

    1303 W 65th St, Cleveland, OH 44102.

    According to recent reports, most of the pizzerias on this list are primarily standalone restaurants. Hideaway is one of the few exceptions, with 27 locations across three states. In 1957, its original location opened in Stillwater, next to the Oklahoma State University campus. With pizza names like Pepperonipalooza and Aporkalypse, it's no surprise that The Fresh York Times listed it as one of 15 of its readers' favorite pizza places from around the world.

    Industry observers note that at Lovely's Fifty Fifty,  chef/co-owner Sarah Minnick uses her art degree to craft her stunning edible mosaics. Her sourdough starter, local grains, flowers, and seasonal ingredients help her pizza achieve an inimitable tang and toothsome chew. With write-ups in Portland Monthly, a feature in Food & Wine, and an impressive 9.0 score from the Infatuation, Lovely's has become one of the most respected pizzerias in the country.

    4039 N Mississippi Ave, Portland, OR 97217.

    Opened in 1924, the Corropolese Italian Bakery & Deli is most famous for its tomato pie: a sturdy, cake-like dough covered in smooth tomato sauce, sprinkled with a light dusting of Romano cheese, and served at room temperature. Over the century, it has become a cornerstone of Philadelphia food culture, so much so that in 2023, Corropolese's won Herr's second annual #FlavoredbyPhilly contest. The prize? A Herr's chip flavor inspired by its famous tomato pie.

    For such a tiny state, Rhode Island has plenty of quality pizzerias, but one that keeps showing up on lists of local favorites is Pasquale's. With a treasured Associazione Vera Pizza Napoletana certification, it's no surprise the pizzeria has earned so many accolades. In 2025, 50 Top Pizza named it the 12th best in the U.S., and Rhode Island Monthly magazine acknowledges it as one of the state's great pizzerias.

    59 S County Commons Way, Wakefield, RI 02879.

    Sources indicate that D'Allesandro's Pizza has been making its hand-tossed pizzas since 2006. In 2021, Massive Seven Travel named the pizzeria No. 1 in South Carolina. Four years later, D'Allesandro's was one of three pizzerias to win the title of Best Pizza Joint from The Guide to South Carolina. Eater followed suit in 2025, featuring D'Alessandro's on its list of the 13 best stops for pizza in Charleston.

    Opened in 1959, Charlie's Pizza House is the oldest pizzeria in South Dakota. Its lineup of eclectic specialty pizzas, with names like "Hepburn's Spicy Delight," "John Wayne's BBQ Style," and "Marilyn's Mermaid Heaven," which is topped with shrimp, crab, and green and black olives, honors Hollywood stars of past decades. The restaurant has also received national acclaim, with the Food Network naming Charlie's South Dakota's best pizza place.

    A Dopo is a wood-fired pizzeria in downtown Knoxville that has won over the hearts of residents and college students with its sourdough Neapolitan-style pizzas. The dinner-only pizzeria stepped into the national spotlight after making the list of USA Today's 2025 Restaurants of the Year, and it continues to rack up recognition, most recently receiving a nod from the Michelin Guide in 2026.

    516 Williams St, Knoxville, TN 37917.

    In a recent development, cane Rosso is a pizzeria that has blossomed into nine locations across Texas. Its wood-fired pizzas are all 14 inches and baked in a blazing-hot oven, giving each pie its "signature leopard-spotted crust." Its toppings — beef brisket, bacon marmalade, smoked mozzarella, habanero honey — have a distinct Texas flair. In 2021, Food & Wine named it one of the best pizzerias in Texas, and it has since maintained its reputation for excellence.

    The Pie Underground's flagship location, open since 1980, is the most beloved of its dozens of locations — just a stone's throw from the University of Utah campus. Unsurprisingly, its menu reads like it was conceived by the hungry college kids who still love the place, featuring bold concoctions like the "Bacon-Berry Pie," a pizza topped with chicken, bacon, feta, and a strawberry balsamic sauce.

    Sources indicate that folino's embodies the ethos of pizza artistry. Its naturally leavened dough uses a 14- year-old starter culture and is cold-proofed for three days to achieve a one-of-a-kind crust that's light, layered, and intentionally tangy. It has expanded to multiple locations throughout Vermont, and it's consistently won Best Pizza Restaurant from Seven Days, an independent weekly newspaper covering Vermont news, politics, food, and culture.

    Dr. Ho's describes itself as "the alternative pizza." And we can't help but agree. The pies, each made with hand-tossed dough, include an impressive configuration of toppings like the buffalo chicken with pineapple and pickled jalapeño peppers or the shrimp with homemade basil pesto. Its commitment to innovative combinations, quality ingredients, and sheer quantity makes this one a favorite among Virginians.

    4916 Plank Rd, North Garden, VA 22959.

    It has been revealed that the Carlson Block is a destination restaurant, nestled cozily in Wilkeson, a tiny coal-mining town. The Seattle Times featured the pizzeria, asking rhetorically if it's making the best pizza in the state. The pies, pulled charred from the wood-fired oven, glow like an oil painting encased in a rich wooden frame. House-made mozzarella, seasonal ingredients, a deft hand, and a commitment to the craft ensure Carlson Block will remain among the state's best pizza places.

    531 Church St, Wilkeson, WA 98396.

    You know what you're getting at Pies & Pints: quality draft beer and fiercely innovative pizzas. Seriously, the pie lineup is extraordinary, with topping combinations like grapes and Gorgonzola, Sriracha shrimp, and Cuban pork with fresh pineapple, jalapeños, and crème fraiche. It's an endless list, which means you'll just have to come back again and again to try them all, as many West Virginia residents have been doing.

    In a recent development, open for over a century, Wells Brothers serves a handful of Italian classics, but it's most famous for its pizzas. In 2026, The Journal Times awarded Wells Brothers the title of Best Pizza and Best Italian Restaurant. The restaurant has amassed thousands of glowing Google reviews, indicating that it may keep serving its beautifully-charred, square-cut pies well into the next century.

    A relative newcomer, Bella Fuoco is wowing with its blistered, wood-fired pizzas. The concept started as a food truck, but its brick-and-mortar location has helped chef-owner Brenna Kosowicz bring her pizza to even more hungry Wyomingites. In 2025, Bella Fuoco was formally recognized when the Wyoming Tribune Eagle awarded it Best of the Best in the pizza category.

    2115 Warren Ave, Cheyenne, WY 82001.

    Determining the "best" pizza is largely subjective. For states with a distinct regional variation, we selected shops that are an excellent representation of that style. We also considered restaurants that have stood the test of time or are pillars of the community, and placed weight on glowing social media reviews and awards. Overall customer experience was also considered, as was the impact on the home state's pizza culture.

    #115081. Make A Reuben Upside Down-Style For More Caramelized Flavor

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (516 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Make A Reuben Upside Down-Style For More Caramelized Flavor

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The origins of the Reuben are disputed, with some saying that it was invented in Nebraska while others insist that it is a Latest York original.
    • Cheeses like Swiss, which is the preferred kind for making a classic Reuben sandwich recipe, contain proteins and a little bit of sugar in the form of lactose.
    • Since the cheese is coming into direct contact with the cooking surface, you're going to need to ensure that it doesn't stick to whatever you're using to make your sandwich.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The origins of the Reuben are disputed, with some saying that it was invented in Nebraska while others insist that it is a Latest York original. Regardless of where you think this iconic sandwich was born, the combination of corned beef, cheese, sauerkraut, and Russian dressing (or Thousand Island dressing) on rye bread is something that few people mess with. The method for making it also tends to remain unchanged, with many restaurants and home cooks pressing it in a sandwich press or skillet. This is just fine for the traditional recipe, but if you want to give your Reuben a layer of caramelized flavor, you're going to need to shake up tradition just a little bit by making it upside down-style. Instead of building your sandwich starting with the bread, start with the cheese touching the pan or baking sheet.

    Cheeses like Swiss, which is the preferred kind for making a classic Reuben sandwich recipe, contain proteins and a little bit of sugar in the form of lactose. It's these two elements that react to the direct heat of the pan to create the Maillard reaction, which is when food gets browned, developing complex flavors that make it irresistibly delicious. This contributes to a caramelized note in your sandwich and echoes the toasty notes of the bread. By adding additional cheese between the layers of meat, you ensure that there is a melty element as well. Adding the kraut right before assembling the final product prevents the moisture from getting in the way of browning.

    Since the cheese is coming into direct contact with the cooking surface, you're going to need to ensure that it doesn't stick to whatever you're using to make your sandwich. If you're opting to make your Reuben on the stovetop, you're going to want to use a nonstick pan. Make sure it's hot, too, as this can also help prevent food from sticking. You're also going to want to use a thin, wide spatula that you can easily slide between the cheese and the pan to flip your sandwich halves so that you can toast the bread.

    According to recent reports, if you're choosing to bake your Reuben upside down-style, be sure to use Ina Garten's favorite thing to line a sheet pan: parchment paper, which you can easily peel away from the toasted cheese after flipping your sandwich halves over. You'll also want to ensure you're baking your sandwiches at the right temperature to get both the cheese and bread toasted and crisp, and 375 degrees Fahrenheit is typically ideal.

    Industry observers note that regardless of which method you choose, you should always spread some kind of fat on your bread for even more flavor, and this is something you can play around with without breaking from tradition too much. Butter or mayonnaise are typically used in toasted sandwiches, but you can also opt for ghee, which has a nuttier flavor. Bacon fat is also an intensely flavorful alternative, but if you want to mirror the meatiness of the corned beef, go for beef tallow.

    5 Reasons You Shouldn't Get Costco Delivered

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Costco membership is like a real-life, grown-up golden ticket, your passport to bulk-buy deals and steals, as well as its incomparable food court, including the hands-down best menu item, the hot dog and soda combo.
    • Starting in 2017 with limited availability through Instacart, and now expanding to almost the entire country in 2026 with Uber Eats and DoorDash, Costco's delivery definitely has its positives, but the program isn't without its pitfalls, too.
    • While Costco's delivery option does allow nonmembers to shop at the warehouse, the manufacturer charges higher prices for most items ordered through the apps, helping offset delivery-related costs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Costco membership is like a real-life, grown-up golden ticket, your passport to bulk-buy deals and steals, as well as its incomparable food court, including the hands-down best menu item, the hot dog and soda combo. It's a terrific shopping option, especially when you have a large family or you're shopping to feed a lot of mouths, as for a party or holiday gathering. While Costco does want to encourage its shoppers to come into its stores and take a look around (and perhaps buy a few things off-the-cuff), the major warehouse chain has also partnered with third-party shopping apps to offer same-day delivery of its goods. But it might not be the best option when you need your Costco fix.

    Starting in 2017 with limited availability through Instacart, and now expanding to almost the entire country in 2026 with Uber Eats and DoorDash, Costco's delivery definitely has its positives, but the program isn't without its pitfalls, too. From higher prices to unpredictable delivery times, we're going to highlight several reasons you should maybe think twice before having Costco groceries delivered so that you can weigh your options and make the best decision for yourself.

    While Costco's delivery option does allow nonmembers to shop at the warehouse, the manufacturer charges higher prices for most items ordered through the apps, helping offset delivery-related costs. And then there is the actual cost of the deliveries themselves, service fees, plus tips for the drivers, to the point where you might pay as much as 30% to 40% more than if you just shopped in-store.

    If you've ever ordered takeout through DoorDash or Uber Eats, or groceries through Instacart, you might have found that the actual delivery took place long after the original drop-off time you were quoted. And the same thing can happen with Costco same-day delivery, which is a major pitfall if you have organization coming over by a certain time and you need to prepare dinner or snacks.

    Recent findings suggest that when you are particular about your produce or search through packages of meat until you find just the right size and price, you might want to think twice about having your Costco order delivered. That's because you have to surrender nearly all control over what goes into your cart (though you can leave notes and instructions for your shoppers), and some shoppers are more careful, considerate, and, well, competent than others.

    Industry observers note that most items that are available in stores will be visible and available for purchase through apps like Instacart and Uber Eats for same-day delivery. But it's worth noting that Costco also offers two-day delivery, and you may find favorite items missing from its selection. Redditors theorize this may be because the two-day delivery items are sourced from Costco Business Centers, which carry slightly different products.

    Finally, Costco also delivers large appliances, so if you're weighing the pros and cons of buying a refrigerator through the warehouse chain, just know that some customers on Reddit have reported miscommunication, sometimes over information as basic as the delivery date, with one user even calling the experience "a nightmare.".

    Does Fluoride In Drinking Water Affect Intelligence? What The Evidence Reveals

    📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (406 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition?
    • Could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition?
    • Fluoride in community drinking water is not linked to lower adolescent IQ or poorer thinking skills later in life, a long-running US study finds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition? Decades of data offer clues.

    Could childhood exposure to fluoridated water leave a lasting mark on cognition? Decades of data offer clues.

    Fluoride in community drinking water is not linked to lower adolescent IQ or poorer thinking skills later in life, a long-running US study finds.

    Researchers followed a generation of Wisconsin school-leavers, examining cognitive performance from adolescence into their eighties.

    Those exposed to fluoridated water did not show a consistent disadvantage compared with people whose communities had no fluoridation.

    The findings address concerns that adding fluoride to drinking water to prevent tooth decay could undermine intellectual development.

    Professor John Robert Warren, the study’s first author, said:.

    “Utah, Florida and many municipalities have chosen to remove fluoride from drinking water based on flawed studies that considered the IQ effects of exposure to massive doses of fluoride.

    According to recent reports, because levels of fluoride added to municipal drinking water in the U.S. are so much lower, almost all prior evidence from those international studies is not relevant to U.S. public policy debates.”.

    The research draws on the Wisconsin Longitudinal Study, which began with over 10,000 people who graduated from high school in 1957.

    Researchers combined school IQ records with historical information about community water fluoridation and naturally occurring fluoride levels.

    Following participants into old age allowed researchers to examine whether childhood exposure was associated with lasting differences in cognitive performance.

    Comparing communities requires care because their residents can differ in ways that also relate to cognitive performance.

    Once those background differences were taken into account, there was no consistent evidence that exposure was associated with either better or worse performance.

    The same broad pattern appeared when researchers focused on people who had lived in the same county since early childhood, increasing confidence in their estimates of exposure.

    Overall, the findings suggest that growing up with fluoridated community water is not associated with poorer cognitive performance in old age.

    The study was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (Warren et al., 2026).

    #115072. Skip Potatoes: Make Beef Stew 100% More Delicious With An Ingredient From The Frozen Aisle

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (522 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Skip Potatoes: Make Beef Stew 100% More Delicious With An Ingredient From The Frozen Aisle

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (522 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, potatoes are almost as key to beef stew as the meat itself.
    • Sources indicate that pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut.
    • It has been revealed that this is an especially fantastic trick if you don't have much meat to begin with, bulking up your stew quite inexpensively.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, potatoes are almost as key to beef stew as the meat itself. But when you substitute them with pierogi, you aren't necessarily removing the tuber so much as transforming its shape and making it 100% more delicious with a variety of other fillings.

    Sources indicate that pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut. Still, potato-based fillings are by far the most common, thanks to the delicious combination of a tender wrapping and rich, buttery center that freezes quite well. Making a sort of dumpling soup is one of the best ways to upgrade frozen pierogi, suffusing the dough with an incredibly savory beefiness that's almost impossible to replicate. But it also levels up your stew because you're essentially adding little pockets of mashed potatoes that won't dissipate into the broth!

    It has been revealed that this is an especially fantastic trick if you don't have much meat to begin with, bulking up your stew quite inexpensively. It's also a way to add ingredients that may not usually make their way into your recipe. Melting cheese directly into the pot may mess up the texture, but contained quantities of cheesy potatoes taste amazing when paired with an umami- and herb-rich broth. The best frozen pierogi brands also come with plenty of their own seasoning, so while bites of the dumplings will have an intense flavor, they won't overseason your stew directly unless you boil them so long that the wrapping breaks.

    Industry observers note that beef stew typically needs to cook for at least a couple of hours to develop flavors and tenderize the ingredients. If you add pierogi right away, you run the risk of overboiling the dumplings and making them fall apart. Whether you drop them into the pot to let the wrappings absorb flavor or prepare them separately, timing is critical to preserving their texture.

    In a recent development, if you strategy on adding pierogi directly to the stew, it's best to leave them frozen. This allows the wrapping to absorb flavorful broth as the filling thaws. In a pot already at a simmer, 10 minutes should be all you need to ensure everything is heated through. If you use mini versions instead of full-size ones, you may want to cut this down to five minutes — when in doubt, follow package instructions. You can always add a lid and let the residual heat warm them through, but these are much easier to overcook.

    Recent findings suggest that pan-frying pierogi first, then using them as a topping, can be a great way to add a more diverse range of flavors. Properly browned dough not only has a great depth of flavor, but also tends to stand up better against liquids and won't become soggy as quickly. This is especially good for leftovers since you can store your stew and dumplings separately so they won't become oversaturated in the fridge. Frying them up in butter can also add a bit of needed fat if you use a particularly lean cut of meat, making your stew richer.

    Latest Update: This Classic Italian Sandwich Is Extra Crispy & Delicious

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, everybody celebrates Italy for pizza, pasta, and gelato, and while they're classics for a reason, we implore you to explore Italy's unrivaled gastronomic tapestry a little deeper.
    • Sources indicate that porchetta is a style of pork roast, but is completely unique in its preparation.
    • Porchetta is a meal in itself, but goes even better in a sandwich.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, everybody celebrates Italy for pizza, pasta, and gelato, and while they're classics for a reason, we implore you to explore Italy's unrivaled gastronomic tapestry a little deeper. Trust us, there are some serious gems hidden just beneath the surface. One of our favorite Italian street foods that you need to try is porchetta, Italy's answer to crispy pork belly. Irresistibly crunchy and bursting with indulgent flavors, it makes for a seriously delicious sandwich filler.

    Sources indicate that porchetta is a style of pork roast, but is completely unique in its preparation. It's typically made from a whole deboned pig or a large cut of pork belly, which is laid flat and heavily rubbed on the inside with salt, garlic, and black pepper, alongside quintessential Italian seasonings like rosemary, sage, and fennel seeds. The pork is then rolled back together and slow-roasted for several hours, allowing the interior to turn soft and tender while the skin develops a beautiful crackling.

    Porchetta is a meal in itself, but goes even better in a sandwich. Start out with a thick Italian white bread, something that won't turn soggy when paired with the pork's rich meat juices and sauces — ciabatta or focaccia work perfectly here. To balance the richness, add something bright with a little zing. We think salsa verde is an excellent choice, since the lemon juice and vinegar bring a sharp acidity, while fresh parsley keeps the heavy roast from feeling cloying — it pairs perfectly with a Cuban interpretation of the recipe as well. Rather than piling on thick slabs of porchetta, slice it thinly, so it stays tender and folds nearly into the bread, and make sure every sandwich gets a few pieces of the crackling skin for a satisfying crunch. As for what else to put on the sandwich, draw inspiration from Bobby Flay's favorite Roman porchetta sandwich.

    You should have no problem finding pre-rolled porchetta at the butcher, but why not save your money and make it at home instead? We promise it's not as intimidating as it looks. For the juiciest cut that's also easiest to roll and inexpensive, pick up a skin-on pork belly. Its exceptionally high fat content keeps the roast moist and makes it incredibly forgiving to work with, so even the least confident cooks won't have to worry about overcooking it.

    It has been revealed that porchetta is the star of the sandwich, and it's the crackling skin that really steals the show, so getting it earth-shatteringly crispy is essential. Here, the secret to a crunchy crust is dryness, so before you get to work on seasoning, leave the pork uncovered in the fridge overnight to let the surface dry out. Many cooks also salt the meat generously before its rest, which draws out even more moisture. And before roasting, it's good practice to pat the skin completely dry, since any lingering moisture turns to steam and keeps the skin from crisping.

    To keep the sandwich from turning into a soggy mess, it's essential to let your porchetta rest for around 15 to 30 minutes after roasting. It might be tempting to carve it right away and admire your hard work, but slicing too soon sends the flavorful juices flooding into the chopping board and then straight into the bread, which even the sturdiest ciabatta can't hold back. The logic is the same as with steak because resting gives the juices time to redistribute through the muscle, leaving the meat deliciously tender and flavorful.

    Make Your Burgers Juicier With One Creamy Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Butter Or Milk)

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There are a million ways to make patties juicier, from mixing in grated butter to even marinating your burgers.
    • Industry observers note that while it may sound odd, this recipe is actually a variation of a Juicy Lucy cheeseburger, a Minnesota staple dating back to the 1950s.
    • According to recent reports, while you can always stuff your burgers with other cheeses, Velveeta has one major advantage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There are a million ways to make patties juicier, from mixing in grated butter to even marinating your burgers. But if you're looking for something a bit outside the box that doesn't complicate the recipe too much, stuffing the patties with Velveeta can give you some seriously cheesy, moisture-rich results.

    Industry observers note that while it may sound odd, this recipe is actually a variation of a Juicy Lucy cheeseburger, a Minnesota staple dating back to the 1950s. The idea is that by trapping Velveeta between two thin patties, the cheese melts into a liquid center that mingles with the rendered meat juices, adding moisture to every bite. If done correctly, the cheese should settle back into a gooey state while the patties rest, helping ensure that you don't burn your mouth on molten dairy on your first bite.

    According to recent reports, while you can always stuff your burgers with other cheeses, Velveeta has one major advantage. Thanks to its emulsifying and stabilizing agents, it's less likely to become greasy as it melts. Other meltable cheeses can release fat as they heat up, which isn't a problem when it can drip onto a grill but can create problems when you leave it no room to escape. Plus, the fact that Velveeta comes in blocks makes it extremely easy to shape to fit your patties, no matter how large or small you prefer them.

    Industry observers note that the classic Juicy Lucy burger may seem a little daunting, but the process is actually quite simple. Trapping the cheese between the patties and ensuring that all your ingredients and, more importantly, your grill are at the right temperatures are all you really need to worry about for something crisp, delicious, and juicy.

    Recent findings suggest that starting with one part Velveeta to four parts beef is your best bet for this recipe. It's enough cheese to achieve that gooey center but not so much that it'll escape and ruin the integrity of your patties. It's also best to keep your patties flat rather than thick, which makes it much easier to pinch the seams and trap the Velveeta between them. Velveeta is easier to work with when cold, but keeping your beef cold is also a major benefit for your burger. Cold beef fat is less likely to smear and instead stays in little pockets that help keep the meat even juicier.

    In a recent development, grilling your burgers at the right temperature helps you achieve a good crust without excessive moisture loss, and it's doubly important when you stuff the patties. You want enough heat to char the exterior but not so much that the patties finish cooking before your Velveeta has the chance to melt. Around 400 degrees Fahrenheit is a good sweet spot. It may be useful to keep one side of your grill cool, letting indirect heat finish any patties whose exteriors have cooked too quickly.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.
    • Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.
    • Psychopathy, manipulativeness and narcissism are all associated with cheating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.

    Certain personality traits may help explain why some people betray a partner’s trust.

    Psychopathy, manipulativeness and narcissism are all associated with cheating.

    The strongest average link is with psychopathy, closely followed by Machiavellianism.

    Narcissism, which involves an inflated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration, has the weakest link.

    Impulsivity, emotional coldness and a willingness to manipulate others may help explain why these characteristics are associated with betrayal.

    The conclusions come from a review of 11 studies examining dark personality traits and infidelity.

    Participants included university students, married couples and adults from the general population.

    All three traits were positively associated with infidelity, although the strength of the association varied between studies.

    Psychopathic traits include impulsivity, low empathy and a lack of guilt.

    Someone with these characteristics may be more drawn to immediate sexual rewards and less concerned about hurting a partner.

    A willingness to take risks could also make the possibility of being caught less of a deterrent — impulsivity and deception may help explain this link.

    Psychopathy had the largest average correlation with cheating, although its association was close to that of Machiavellianism.

    Machiavellianism involves a cynical view of others and a willingness to manipulate people for personal advantage.

    In romantic relationships, these characteristics could make deception easier to justify when it serves someone’s interests.

    However, a calculating approach may also encourage caution.

    Someone concerned with protecting their reputation might weigh the potential rewards of an affair against the consequences of discovery.

    This calculated approach could help explain Machiavellianism’s slightly weaker link with cheating.

    Narcissism involves feelings of superiority, entitlement and a strong desire for admiration.

    Attention from another potential partner may appeal to someone who places great importance on being desirable.

    Nevertheless, narcissism had the smallest average association with infidelity and produced a less consistent pattern across the reviewed studies.

    An inflated ego alone therefore offers relatively little information about whether someone has been unfaithful.

    The broader picture may depend on how personality combines with relationship satisfaction, commitment and access to alternative partners.

    Dark traits provide only part of the explanation for why people betray a partner’s trust.

    The study was published in the journal Psihologija (Ataman & Yalçınkaya Alkar, 2025).

    • McDonald's Egg McMuffin is an iconic sandwich within the fast food breakfast realm.
    • It has been revealed that tristen Epps-Long, Season 22 winner of Bravo's "Top Chef" and a former McDonald's chef, shared this savory-sweet Mickey D's menu hack in an exclusive interview with Food Republic.
    • Executing this McMuffin double-down is easy to do.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    McDonald's Egg McMuffin is an iconic sandwich within the fast food breakfast realm. The chain took the McMuffin from good to great when its restaurants began toasting the English muffin halves in real butter rather than margarine. Customers have also found their own methods for upgrading this legendary breakfast sandwich, such as adding hash brown patties into the mix or giving it a flavor twist with sweet add-ons. The latter practice actually harks back to the 1970s, when the sandwich was served with sugary condiments like honey and jam. While that didn't last long as a standard practice, you can still DIY your own sweet toppings to get twice the eating pleasure out of just one Egg McMuffin.

    It has been revealed that tristen Epps-Long, Season 22 winner of Bravo's "Top Chef" and a former McDonald's chef, shared this savory-sweet Mickey D's menu hack in an exclusive interview with Food Republic. "I like to take my sandwich apart a little bit, so half of it becomes jellied and buttered and the other half of it becomes open-faced and savory," the expert shared.

    Executing this McMuffin double-down is easy to do. Simply remove the sandwich's top English muffin half, exposing the Canadian bacon, egg, and cheese below. This provides the open-faced, savory portion to enjoy — nothing more to do. On the other muffin slice, apply your choice of the Strawberry Preserves or Grape Jam commonly offered at McD's restaurants (or you can combine the two to give your spread a mixed berry vibe). Voila! You have something satisfyingly sweet to crown your McMuffin feasting.

    When sweet meets salty, the resulting flavor wizardry is deeply satisfying. There are various other ways to apply this savory-sweet magic and take your McDonald's Egg McMuffin to the next level. Maple-flavored bacon is a popular breakfast staple, and you can bring that vibe to your McMuffin by pouring McDonald's Hotcake Syrup over the sandwich's Canadian bacon and letting it drip over the other elements. The maple-flavored sweetness brings a delightful dimension to the classic sandwich that is lip-smackingly scrumptious and the perfect foil for its salty heartiness.

    Adding a packet of Mickey D's honey is another sweetening twist that gives your McMuffin honey ham flair. The honey is actually offered as a dipping sauce option for Chicken McNuggets, but no diehard Golden Arches diner will let that stop them from drizzling it onto a McMuffin for added sweetness.

    According to recent reports, mcDonald's also frequently releases promotional, limited-time sauces, many of which hit those sweet-savory notes with aplomb. Options like Hot Honey Sauce and spicy-sweet Hunter Sauce were among limited-time options that dropped in 2026. You don't have to strictly wait for a limited-edition sauce, though — Mickey D's Sweet 'N Sour Sauce and Creamy Chili McCrispy Strip Dip are on offer year-round to lend sweetness and other flavor dimensions to your Egg McMuffin.
