    In a recent development, neurodivergent kids aren’t the only ones who struggle with changing routines or newly introduced life phases. Adults can feel overwhelmed by transitions, too.

    Whether starting a new job, moving to a new town, or sending a child off to college, transitions are equal parts exciting and uncomfortable for neurodivergent individuals.

    The struggle often looks different in children and adults, but the demand is much the same: Stop what you are doing, shift your attention, figure out the next step, manage your emotions, and move into a different role, task, place, or expectation. The bigger the transition, the harder it feels.

    Typical transitions include returning to work after a vacation, adjusting to a new schedule, shifting from work to parenting mode, navigating relationship changes, and recovering from illness or injury.

    [Free Download: Get Control of Your Life and Schedule].

    From the outside, the response of an adult with ADHD may look like procrastination, avoidance, irritability, disorganization, or poor follow-through. Internally, they are likely dealing with anxiety, emotional overload, decision fatigue, time blindness, or the frustration of knowing exactly what needs to be done but struggling to begin.

    “I struggle so badly with transitions (they feel almost literally painful) that I spend up to five hours in a state of crippling inertia before handling a task that needs to be done,” wrote one woman with ADHD in a social media post, pleading for help.

    Transitions can be especially difficult when they involve uncertainty. A new job may bring excitement and anxiety about performance. A vacation may feel adventurous and overwhelming. Even a positive life change can feel unsettling when structure falls away.

    “I don’t travel much,” says Layla, an ADDitude reader from California. “Transitions are hard for me.”.

    [Get This Free Download: Finish Your To-Do List Today].

    Shave the rough edges off transitions by doing the following seven things:.

    Sources indicate that most importantly, adults with ADHD should keep in mind that embracing change easily is not necessarily a sign of maturity. Feelings of anxiety around transitions may just mean that your brain needs more preview, structure, recovery, and support to move from one demand to the next.

    ADHD in Midlife & Beyond: 5 Big Research Findings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Additudemag

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • “What helped someone with ADHD in their 20s is necessarily going to help them in their 60s, 70s, and 80s.”.
    • The experience of ADHD in midlife and older age is largely undocumented but not unimportant.
    • An estimated 66% of adults with ADHD ages 45 to 54 have no recorded diagnosis, according to an analysis of UK health records.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    “What helped someone with ADHD in their 20s is necessarily going to help them in their 60s, 70s, and 80s.”.

    The experience of ADHD in midlife and older age is largely undocumented but not unimportant.

    An estimated 66% of adults with ADHD ages 45 to 54 have no recorded diagnosis, according to an analysis of UK health records. Missed diagnoses and misdiagnoses make research on this population difficult — but not impossible.

    Amber John, Ph.D., a researcher at the University of Liverpool, reviewed studies on how the experience of ADHD changes with age during her November 2026 ADDitude webinar, “Aging with ADHD: Latest Research Findings in Midlife and Beyond.”.

    Below are some of the themes John highlighted and what they suggest about the support adults with ADHD need in midlife and beyond.

    In clinical interviews, adults with ADHD recalled feeling different growing up but being unable to explain why. A diagnosis helped them see those experiences in a different light.

    It has been revealed that “These experiences that previously might have seemed disconnected, for many, started to form this more understandable pattern,” John remarked. “And that could really change the meaning that someone gives to those past experiences, particularly where they had just been viewed as evidence of personal failings.”.

    [Read: The Transformative Power of an ADHD Diagnosis for Older Women].

    According to recent reports, many people with ADHD develop painstaking routines and coping strategies to manage symptoms. The effort it takes to keep those routines going often goes unseen and can fuel burnout.

    Recent findings suggest that “This raises a really important question about what it is that we actually mean when we say someone is functioning well,” John said. “Understanding someone’s support needs really means that we need to ask about the cost of managing.”.

    Industry observers note that the experience of ADHD changes as life circumstances change. Menopause, caring for aging parents, and retirement can affect how symptoms play out in daily life and disrupt routines that have helped people cope for decades.

    “A way that somebody is using to manage or to cope that’s worked in one period of life might become less useful when health, or demands, or available support changes,” John said.

    According to recent reports, [Read: I Feared I Had Alzheimer’s. It Turns Out It Was Undiagnosed ADHD.].

    Sources indicate that in doctors’ offices and workplaces, people with ADHD often shoulder the burden of explaining their needs and advocating for basic support. They can put considerable effort into managing their symptoms and still face barriers to getting care or participating at work.

    “There is a limit to focusing on individual-level coping because a person can put really substantial effort into managing whilst the environment actually continues to make participation difficult,” John stated.

    Sources indicate that john’s research highlights the need for ADHD support that adapts as people’s circumstances change. We shouldn’t assume that “what helped someone with ADHD in their 20s is necessarily going to help them in their 60s, 70s, and 80s,” she remarked.

    For more on ADHD in midlife and beyond, watch the full webinar at additu.de/111726.

    • You might struggle to find the right words to tell your family or friends just how much you care, or maybe you’re not sure what’s appropriate to say to your colleagues or business partner.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanksgiving is a time to reflect on everything—and everyone—you’re thankful for, but expressing those feelings, especially to the people who matter most, isn’t always easy.

    You might struggle to find the right words to tell your family or friends just how much you care, or maybe you’re not sure what’s appropriate to say to your colleagues or business partner. You’re bound to brighten someone’s day no matter what you say, but it can be helpful to have a few suggestions on hand.

    According to recent reports, this guide will help you craft meaningful Thanksgiving greetings for every crucial person in your life. From warm and sentimental messages to professional and appreciative ones, we can help you find the perfect words to share gratitude and reflect on your connections.

    You may associate Thanksgiving with turkey and all the trimmings — but it’s really time to celebrate the people you love. Whether it’s your family, lifelong friends, or the colleagues you see every day, Thanksgiving is a perfect excuse to tell them how much you care.

    A heartfelt message doesn’t have to be complicated. A few sincere words can go a long way! Whether you’re writing a card, sending a text, or sharing your thoughts in person, taking the time to say something meaningful highlights you care.

    Here’s how you can share thoughtful greetings and make everyone in your life feel truly special this holiday season.

    Sources indicate that for many people, Thanksgiving is a time to gather with family, making it the perfect time to let them know how much they mean to you. Family often gives us our strongest foundation — offering love, support, and shared traditions that make life richer. A quick text or call can go a long way in showing your gratitude, and you might consider saying something like:.

    Sources indicate that 1. “Wishing you a Thanksgiving filled with love, laughter, and all our favorite traditions. I’m so thankful for the memories we’ve made together.”.

    Sources indicate that 2. “This Thanksgiving, I feel so lucky to have such a wonderful family. Thank you for being my rock through all the ups and downs.”.

    Industry observers note that 3. “Happy Thanksgiving! I’m grateful every day that you’re my family.”.

    It has been revealed that include a shared memory: Mention something specific that connects you to the recipient. For example, “I’ll never forget last year’s Thanksgiving dinner when we all laughed until we cried. Here’s to making more memories like that!”.

    In a recent development, focus on their unique qualities: Highlight what you admire about them. You might say, “Your kindness and generosity inspire me every day, and I’m so thankful to have you in my life.”.

    Express anticipation for the future: If you’re celebrating together, add a line about how much you’re looking forward to it, such as, “I can’t wait to see you and enjoy Mom’s famous pumpkin pie together!”.

    Friends are the family we choose, and Thanksgiving is the perfect opportunity to let them know how much they mean to you. Whether it’s the friend who always knows how to make you laugh, the one who listens when you need to talk, or the group that feels like home, these connections deserve to be celebrated.

    In a recent development, 4. “Happy Thanksgiving! Your friendship means the world to me. Thank you for bringing so much joy into my life.”.

    It has been revealed that 5. “Here’s to great friends, good food, and gratitude. I’m so thankful for the laughs and support you’ve shared with me this year.”.

    Industry observers note that 6. “Wishing you a Thanksgiving as amazing as you are. Thank you for always being there and making life so much better.”.

    Acknowledge their impact on your life: Mention specific ways they’ve helped or supported you. For example, “I’ll always be grateful for the time you helped me through a rough patch. Your kindness made all the difference.”.

    Sources indicate that celebrate shared moments: Bring up a memory that captures the essence of your friendship. For example, “I’m so thankful for our road trip this year — it was one of the best vacations of my life!”.

    In a recent development, show excitement for future intends: If you have plans to celebrate together or see each other soon, include that in your message. For example, “I can’t wait to watch the Thanksgiving parade with you this year — it’s my favorite tradition!”.

    💙 In her Gratitude Masterclass, Tamara Levitt teaches you to unlock the transformative power of this life-changing practice.

    Your colleagues play an crucial role in your daily life. Whether it’s collaborating on projects, sharing laughs during lunch breaks, or supporting each other through challenges, the relationships you build at work can make your life much more rewarding.

    Expressing appreciation to colleagues doesn’t have to be complicated — and if done well, it can foster a more collaborative work environment. (In the meantime, here are 13 tips for effective communication at work.).

    7. “Happy Thanksgiving! I’m so grateful to work alongside you. Your dedication and positivity make a difference every day.”.

    8. “Wishing you and your loved ones a joyful and peaceful Thanksgiving. I’m thankful for your hard work and the kindness you bring to the workplace.”.

    9. “I truly appreciate everything you do and the impact you have on our team. Have a great (and relaxing) Thanksgiving!”.

    It has been revealed that acknowledge specific contributions: Highlight something they’ve done that stood out to you. For example, “Your leadership on our last project really inspired me. I’m grateful to have you as a colleague.”.

    Recent findings suggest that reflect on shared experiences: If you’ve had a particularly positive moment working together, bring it up. You could say, “I’ll always remember how we pulled together for the massive presentation last month — it was such a team effort!”.

    It has been revealed that use a friendly, conversational tone: While professionalism is important, don’t be afraid to let your personality show. For example, “Hope you get to kick back and relax this Thanksgiving — you’ve earned it after all the hard work this year!” And if you work with a distributed team, try putting something cheerful in a group email or on Slack or Teams to build camaraderie.

    Industry observers note that you’re probably thankful for your career, and if you provide a service of any kind, your clients are a substantial part of that. A thoughtful Thanksgiving message can show your appreciation, set the tone for a continued relationship, and acknowledge the role they play in your success. Plus, when you take the time to say “thank you,” you’re building goodwill, deepening trust, and showing that they matter beyond their business.

    In a recent development, 10. “Happy Thanksgiving! We are truly grateful for your trust and partnership. Working with you has been a pleasure, and we wish you a season filled with happiness and success.”.

    11. “As we reflect on the past year, we’re reminded how fortunate we are to work with incredible clients like you. Thank you for your support, and we wish you a happy Thanksgiving!”.

    12. “Wishing you a wonderful Thanksgiving! We deeply appreciate your business and look forward to continuing our partnership in the year ahead.”.

    Mention specific successes or collaborations: For example, “Your trust during our product launch earlier this year meant so much to us. Thank you for helping us achieve that milestone!”.

    In a recent development, express excitement about future opportunities: Share your enthusiasm for continuing the relationship. You could say, “We’re excited to see what we can achieve together in the coming year!”.

    Incorporate a small token of appreciation: If appropriate, consider pairing your message with a thoughtful gift, such as a branded item, a box of treats, or a donation made in their name to a charitable cause.

    💙 Learn the secret to stronger connections with our Relationship with Others series.

    Instead of “Happy Thanksgiving,” you could use phrases like “Wishing you a Thanksgiving filled with love, laughter, and cherished memories” or “I hope you have a great holiday, and a few slices of pie.” “Happy Thanksgiving” is still a classic, but a more personal phrase may help your message stand out.

    In a recent development, for someone you’re especially thankful for, you can go a step further by expressing how much they mean to you, maybe including some specific details or examples. The key is to speak from the heart.

    Personalizing your message starts with thinking about your relationship with the person. For family, consider mentioning shared traditions or memories that make Thanksgiving special for you. For example, you could write, “I’ll always remember how we all used to watch football together before gathering around grandma’s table.” Acknowledging shared experiences shows how much you value the bond you have with them.

    For friends, focus on the qualities that make your friendship unique. A message like, “Your kindness and sense of humor have made this year so much better — thank you for being such a wonderful friend” can brighten their day.

    Sources indicate that when it comes to colleagues, a professional yet warm approach works best. Mention how much you value their hard work, teamwork, or support, like, “Your dedication and positivity inspire me every day. I’m so grateful to have you as a colleague.”.

    Industry observers note that when crafting Thanksgiving messages for clients or business partners, it’s notable to strike the right balance between professional and personal. The tone should reflect gratitude for their trust and collaboration while maintaining a polished and respectful vibe. For example, a message like, “We’re deeply thankful for your continued support and trust in us. Wishing you and your loved ones a wonderful Thanksgiving,” conveys both professionalism and warmth.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’ve worked closely on a specific project or achieved significant milestones together, mentioning those can add a thoughtful touch. For instance, “This year, your partnership helped us achieve some truly amazing things, and we’re so grateful for your contributions. Here’s to more success in the coming year!” This approach not only expresses thanks but also highlights the value of your ongoing relationship.

    One simple way to incorporate gratitude practices into your Thanksgiving celebration is to go around the table and ask everyone to share what they’re grateful for.

    According to recent reports, you can also write thank you notes to people who have made an impact on your year. These don’t have to be lengthy — even a few sentences can make someone feel appreciated. If you’re celebrating with family or friends, consider surprising them with a small note expressing why you’re thankful for them.

    Recent findings suggest that you might also consider giving back to your community, which can be incredibly fulfilling. Volunteering at a local shelter, donating to a food bank, or helping a neighbor in need are all ways to show gratitude through action. These practices not only enhance your Thanksgiving but also leave a positive impact on those around you. To cultivate a stronger sense of gratitude, try these eight tips.

    According to recent reports, thanksgiving cards are a thoughtful way to share your gratitude, and adding a creative touch makes them even more special. One idea is to include a photo — this could be a family picture, a snapshot of your team at work, or even an image of a past Thanksgiving celebration. Photos instantly make a card feel more personal and nostalgic.

    It has been revealed that you could also include a short, heartfelt message or even a simple poem about gratitude and the season. If you enjoy crafting, consider making a DIY card with autumnal designs like leaves, pumpkins, or warm color palettes. Adding small details like handwritten notes or a ribbon tie are nice too.

    For digital cards, don’t be afraid to use design tools or templates to create something unique. A thoughtful e-card can still feel personal if you take the time to craft a meaningful message. What matters most is the care and effort you put into creating and sending it.

    Thanksgiving greetings are about more than just words — they’re a way to connect, show gratitude, and spread warmth during this time of year. By tailoring your messages and including a personal touch, you’ll make each greeting that much more meaningful.

    A good Thanksgiving greeting card message names the person and indicates one thing you’re thankful for about them. It can be a single line or a longer note, depending on how well you know them.

    For a close friend or family member, you might write, “Thank you for showing up for me this year. I’m grateful for you today and every day.” For a neighbor or a teacher, something like, “Thank you for being so kind to our family this year. Wishing you a warm and relaxing holiday,” works well.

    It has been revealed that A card gives you more room than a text does, so you can add a memory or a detail only the two of you would know. If you’re stuck, write the way you’d talk to them. A sign-off like “With gratitude” or “Thinking of you” can finish it off.

    #114969. Study: Menstrual Cycle Irregularities Linked to ADHD, Depression, Anxiety in Girls

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1043 w)

    Study: Menstrual Cycle Irregularities Linked to ADHD, Depression, Anxiety in Girls

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1043 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Additudemag

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Menstrual cycle irregularities, like severe menstrual pain and premenstrual symptoms, are associated with mental health conditions in adolescent girls, according to a new study.
    • Several menstrual cycle characteristics, including timing of menarche, cycle regularity, menstrual pain, and severity of premenstrual symptoms, are associated with more common and severe symptoms of depression, anxiety, and ADHD in adolescent girls, according to a recent study published in European Child & Adolescent Psychiatry.1.
    • The longitudinal study followed 5,673 adolescent girls, ages 9 to 11, over a seven-year period, with annual assessments up to ages 14 to 17.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Menstrual cycle irregularities, like severe menstrual pain and premenstrual symptoms, are associated with mental health conditions in adolescent girls, according to a new study.

    Several menstrual cycle characteristics, including timing of menarche, cycle regularity, menstrual pain, and severity of premenstrual symptoms, are associated with more common and severe symptoms of depression, anxiety, and ADHD in adolescent girls, according to a recent study published in European Child & Adolescent Psychiatry.1.

    The longitudinal study followed 5,673 adolescent girls, ages 9 to 11, over a seven-year period, with annual assessments up to ages 14 to 17.

    In a recent development, study participants self-reported the severity of premenstrual symptoms, such as irritability and fatigue, and the intensity of period pain (categorized as mild, moderate, or severe). Findings indicated that severe menstrual pain was associated with higher anxiety, depression, and ADHD symptoms.

    According to recent reports, premenstrual symptoms demonstrated a graded pattern in their association with mental health outcomes. Mild premenstrual symptoms were linked to higher anxiety symptom scores. Moderate premenstrual symptoms were linked to higher anxiety and depression symptom scores. Severe premenstrual symptoms were linked to higher anxiety, depression, and ADHD symptom scores.

    The researchers offered several social and biological factors as potential explanations for these results.

    “Psychosocially, menstrual pain and [premenstrual symptoms] may result in functional impairment – including missed school, disrupted sleep, reduced social participation – which may contribute to emotional distress,” they wrote.

    It has been revealed that the study explained that intense period pain and premenstrual distress may activate inflammatory and pain-sensitivity pathways, increasing vulnerability to anxiety and depression. Researchers also noted that the neurobiological mechanisms for processing pain may overlap with those involved in attention and focus, which could help explain the connection between menstrual pain and ADHD symptoms.

    Researchers also suggested that fluctuating estrogen and progesterone may help to explain the connection between severe premenstrual symptoms and higher anxiety, depression, and ADHD symptom scores. These hormones heavily affect serotonin, dopamine, and GABA in the brain. Serotonin is linked to mood; dopamine controls motivation and reward processing; and GABA is crucial for emotional processing and regulation. When hormones fluctuate before a menstrual cycle, these neurotransmitters are impacted too, which, in turn, may influence symptoms of anxiety, depression, and ADHD.

    Sources indicate that the relationship between ADHD and hormonal fluctuations is a pressing subject for many ADDitude readers with lived experience. In an ADDitude survey of nearly 2,000 women with ADHD, almost one in two respondents stated that hormonal fluctuations had a “life-altering” or “severe” impact on their ADHD.

    “I know that the week before my period I am a complete mess,” Addison, an ADDitude reader, said. “I have to prepare for the fact that my world feels like it’s falling apart emotionally, and I hate the way that I look the most that week. These are weeks I often avoid being with people, as I know I am not the most positive and am the most sensitive.”.

    “I used to have lots of irritability, food cravings, tiredness, and was fuzzy-headed three to four days before my period started,” said Connie, another reader.

    Sources indicate that “I suffer from symptoms like uncontrolled fits of anger and crying spells and feeling extremely overwhelmed the days before my period. I’m even more moody, irritable and have more trouble concentrating,” stated ADDitude reader Elena.

    Moreover, women with ADHD are disproportionately affected by premenstrual disorders with more than 40% of women with ADHD experiencing premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) compared to 3% to 9% of women overall.2, 3 PMDD is also heavily tied to hormonal shifts and mental health.

    Sources indicate that “PMDD is caused by a high sensitivity to fluctuations in estrogen and progesterone, as well as decreases in serotonin – hormonal changes that happen during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle,” wrote Dara Abraham, D.O. in an ADDitude article. “During the luteal phase that follows ovulation, estrogen decreases, as do dopamine, serotonin, and eventually progesterone. These changes cause painful and distressing symptoms until the menstruation begins and hormone levels rise again.”.

    The study also found that irregular menstrual cycles were linked to higher depression and anxiety symptom scores. The longer a girl had been having her menstrual cycles, the stronger the link between irregular periods and depression and anxiety symptoms became. Likewise, earlier age at menarche was associated with higher depression symptom scores.

    While the study focused specifically on early age at menarche, previous research suggests that early puberty more broadly may have an association to ADHD.

    It has been revealed that “Researchers are examining why girls with ADHD have about twice the risk for early puberty, and why autistic girls are up to four times more likely to experience early puberty compared to other children,” wrote Molly Nikolas, Ph.D. in an ADDitude article. “In addition to higher rates of obesity and social stress, which could accelerate the onset of puberty, neurodivergent girls may experience differences in dopamine activity, stress response, and immune and neuroendocrine systems — all of which may affect sexual development.”.

    In a recent development, the researchers listed several limitations to the study. Menstrual cycle characteristics were gathered through an annual self-report, and parents reported mental health symptoms. In addition, the relationship between menstrual characteristics and mental health symptoms may be bidirectional. The researchers also reported the associations were modest and that future studies are needed to further explore the potential social and biological mechanisms involved.

    The study’s authors stated they hope their findings will help healthcare professionals consider menstrual cycle characteristics as potentially meaningful insight when evaluating the mental health of adolescent girls.

    1 Marla, S., Gangaraju, S.H., Nguyen, J. et al. Association between menstrual cycle characteristics and mental health in early adolescence. Eur Child Adolesc Psychiatry 35, 4035–4049 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1007/s00787-026-03163-8.

    2 Team, A. E. (2025). PMDD and ADHD: Understanding the connection and managing symptoms. ADDA – Attention Deficit Disorder Association. https://add.org/pmdd-and-adhd/.

    In a recent development, 3 Pooja Thakrar, Kalyani Bhukar, Rajat Oswal, Premenstrual dysphoric disorder: Prevalence, quality of life and disability due to illness among medical and paramedical students. Journal of Affective Disorders Reports, Volume 4, 2021, 100112, ISSN 2666-9153, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jadr.2021.100112.

    Tech Report: 10 types of breathing exercises and techniques to try

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2242 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that clinically reviewed by Dr.
    • Your boss just dumped a ton of extra work on your desk, your kids’ school just told you they need to dress up as an ancient Greek philosopher tomorrow, a friend is texting about a personal crisis, and the fridge is empty, so you’ve got to fit in a grocery run.
    • In a recent development, when stress builds up and life feels overwhelming, we often forget to just breathe.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

    We all have those days. Your boss just dumped a ton of extra work on your desk, your kids’ school just told you they need to dress up as an ancient Greek philosopher tomorrow, a friend is texting about a personal crisis, and the fridge is empty, so you’ve got to fit in a grocery run. It’s… a lot.

    In a recent development, when stress builds up and life feels overwhelming, we often forget to just breathe. But slowing down to focus on your breath can be a simple way to find calm and feel in control again.

    Breathing exercises give you tools to manage stress, ease anxiety, and even boost your mood. These breathing techniques are quick to learn and can be done almost anywhere, whether you’re sitting in traffic, lying in bed, or taking a quick break at work.

    Recent findings suggest that in this guide, we’ll go through 10 types of breathing exercises, show you how to practice them, and explain how they can help. Here’s where to start.

    According to recent reports, breathing exercises are simple techniques that help you take control of your breath. When we’re stressed or anxious, our breath usually speeds up, which can actually make us feel more anxious. But doing some focused breathing can help interrupt the cycle in a way that naturally calms your body and mind.

    There are lots of techniques, and they each work a little differently or have a particular area of intention. Some breathing exercises are best for reducing anxiety, while others can help improve focus, ease muscle tension, or even prepare you for a good night’s sleep.

    Many people use breathing exercises to help in a challenging moment  or simply as part of a regular daily routine to help them keep stress at bay, sleep better, and make it easier to stay calm and focused throughout the day.

    You may be wondering if something so simple can really solve all your problems. And the answer is no —they can’t fill your shopping cart or complete that work project—but they can support your physical and mental health in more ways than one.

    Reduces stress and anxiety: Breathing exercises calm the body’s stress response, quieting anxiety and helping you feel more centered.

    Improves focus and concentration: Taking a few deep breaths can help sharpen your focus, so you can stay present and engaged.

    Helps manage emotions: Focusing on your breath promotes a sense of calm and control, so you can handle emotions better. Struggling with your emotions? Check out these nine emotional regulation tips.

    Boosts physical health: Certain breathing exercises can help improve lung capacity, circulation, and even immune response.

    Supports better sleep: Breathing exercises like 4–7–8 breathing can help you fall asleep faster and improve the quality of your sleep (these six tips before bed can help too).

    Boosts mood and mental wellbeing: Certain techniques, like resonant breathing (which is when you breathe slowly and evenly, usually around 5-6 breaths per minute), can improve your mood and overall sense of wellbeing.

    Provides a sense of control: Breathing exercises remind you that even in challenging moments, you have the power to calm yourself.

    According to recent reports, when life feels busy or overwhelming, having a variety of breathing exercises in your back pocket can be incredibly helpful. Since each exercise works a bit differently, being familiar with a few means you'll be better able to support yourself in any situation, whether you’re looking to calm down, get focused, or ease into sleep.

    As one of the simplest yet most effective ways to calm your body and mind, this technique is especially useful when you need to relieve stress, feel more grounded, or prepare for a restful night’s sleep. If you’re struggling to sleep well, try pairing breathing with these 10 tips to improve your sleep quality.

    Industry observers note that how to practice: Find a comfortable position, either sitting or lying down. Place one hand on your belly to help you feel each breath as you inhale deeply through your nose, allowing your stomach to rise as you fill your lungs. Hold your breath for a couple of seconds, then slowly exhale through your mouth, feeling your belly fall. Repeat this pattern for about five to ten breaths, letting your body relax with each exhale.

    💙 Learn an easy way to practice deep belly breathing with the Balloon Breath meditation, great for kids and adults!

    This type of breathing can help strengthen your diaphragm and improve your body’s ability to take in oxygen. It can be particularly helpful if you're dealing with respiratory issues or you want to ease physical tension (these six tips can also help).

    It has been revealed that how to practice: Place one hand on your chest and the other right below your ribs. Breathe in deeply through your nose, aiming to move only your diaphragm (your belly should rise while your chest stays relatively still). Exhale slowly through pursed lips, feeling your belly lower. Practice this for about 5–10 minutes.

    A favorite among people who need to manage stress on the go, box breathing helps balance oxygen levels, slow your heart rate, and rapidly shift your body into a calm state, making it ideal for high-stress situations.

    How to practice: Visualize a box where each breath segment represents one side. Inhale slowly through your nose for a count of four as you imagine progressing up the side of the square, hold your breath for another four along the top of the square, exhale for four as you move down the box, then pause for a final count of four to return to the start point. Continue for a few rounds, focusing on maintaining an even rhythm.

    It has been revealed that this technique is designed to calm the nervous system and ease anxiety. It’s particularly useful for winding down at the end of the day, so you're feeling ready for sleep. If you’re looking for more sleep support, check out these eight breathing exercises.

    Recent findings suggest that how to practice: Breathe in through your nose for a count of four, and hold your breath for a count of seven. Breathe out slowly through your mouth for a count of eight, aiming for a gentle, complete exhale. Repeat this sequence three to four times, allowing yourself to fully relax.

    It has been revealed that alternate nostril breathing can help balance energy, ease stress, and improve focus. It’s a great choice when you’re feeling mentally or physically drained and need a quick reset.

    How to practice: Sit in a comfortable position and place your left hand on your knee. With your right thumb, gently close your right nostril and inhale deeply through your left nostril. Close your left nostril with your ring finger, release your right nostril, and exhale fully through the right side. Inhale through the right nostril, close it, then exhale through the left. Continue this alternating pattern 5–10 times.

    💙 Let Mel Mah guide you through an alternate nostril breathing practice during the Immune Strength for Optimal Health session.

    Recent findings suggest that this technique can increase oxygen flow to the lungs, which can be especially helpful if you have respiratory concerns. It’s also calming, so it can ease anxiety and reduce shortness of breath.

    How to practice: Breathe in through your nose for a count of two, then purse your lips as if you’re blowing out a candle and exhale slowly for a count of four. Keep the exhale gentle and controlled. Repeat several times, focusing on making the exhale twice as long as the inhale.

    Sources indicate that the lion’s breath exercise releases tension, particularly in the face and jaw, while also boosting energy and clearing mental fog. It’s an energizing technique that’s great for moments when you feel sluggish or want to improve your mood quickly.

    How to practice: Take a deep breath in through your nose. Next, open your mouth wide, stick out your tongue, and forcefully exhale with a loud “ha” sound. Focus on releasing any tension from your face, jaw, and throat. Repeat 3–5 times, letting yourself feel fully present with the exercise.

    It has been revealed that also known as coherent breathing, resonant breathing can help calm your nervous system and improve heart rate variability, which is an indicator of how your body adapts to stress and recovers. It’s a great technique for anyone looking to manage stress in the long run.

    How to practice: Breathe in deeply for a count of five and then exhale for a count of five, maintaining a steady, slow rhythm. Aim to take about six breaths per minute, or whatever pace feels comfortable, and focus on keeping your breaths even and controlled.

    Recent findings suggest that use this deeply relaxing technique to reduce frustration and tension. It can be particularly helpful for calming your mind before sleep or during moments of stress.

    How to practice: Sit comfortably, close your eyes, and take a deep breath in. As you exhale, make a gentle humming sound, like a bee, and focus on the vibrations in your head and face. Repeat this pattern five to ten times, letting the vibrations soothe your mind.

    💙 Practice the humming bee breath in The Daily Move’s Wake Up Your Voice.

    Sources indicate that breath counting is a mindful technique that brings you into the present moment, as counting the breaths can quiet racing thoughts and promote relaxation. This helps relieve stress and improve your focus.

    According to recent reports, how to practice: Mentally count “one” on the inhale, and then exhale normally. Then count “two” as you breathe to inhale, then silent on the exhale. Keep going all the way up to 10 and then start over again at one. Try this for about 5–10 minutes, focusing on the rhythm of your breathing. If you lose count, start at one again.

    💙 Learn to Count the Breaths with guidance from Jeff Warren and The Daily Trip.

    Practicing breathing exercises daily is the best way to see results. Even just a few minutes every day can help you feel calmer, more focused, and better able to manage whatever stress comes your way.

    In a recent development, many people find that practicing in the morning helps set a positive tone for the day, while an evening practice can be a great way to unwind and relax before bed, so try both to work out what fits best with your life. And if you’re looking to improve your daily routine, check out these tips to build your morning, workday, and evening routines..

    If daily practice feels like too much at first, try starting with just 5–10 minutes a few times a week, as every bit counts toward building a sense of calm and balance.

    Breathing exercises can be very helpful for managing anxiety and even calming a panic attack.

    Industry observers note that when anxiety hits, our breathing often becomes shallow and quick, which can make us feel even more anxious. Practicing slow, deep breathing helps break this cycle, sending a signal to your brain and body that things are okay. Try techniques like deep breathing, box breathing, and 4–7–8 breathing to calm your nervous system during anxious moments.

    It has been revealed that if you struggle with anxiety or panic attacks, learn breathing techniques in a relaxed setting first. Being familiar with the exercises makes it easier to use them when you’re feeling anxious, so you can start to feel in control and more grounded in tougher times.

    Several breathing exercises can be particularly helpful for improving sleep.

    If you’re having trouble sleeping, set aside just a few minutes before bed to practice techniques like 4–7–8 breathing and humming bee breath, as they're known for their calming effects on the nervous system. These exercises can slow down your breathing and heart rate, making it easier to relax and drift off to sleep.

    Surprisingly, certain breathing exercises can support your physical fitness and endurance. Techniques like diaphragmatic breathing, pursed lip breathing, and resonant breathing can improve lung capacity, which can help your body use oxygen more efficiently.

    When your lungs are stronger and your breathing is steady, you can perform your favorite sports and exercises better, whether that’s walking, hitting the gym, football, dancing, or any other way you like to get active.

    Sources indicate that in fact, many pro athletes use breathing techniques to improve their performance and recovery time, so if you want to improve your endurance, try practicing regularly. You can do them either before a workout to warm up your lungs or afterward to help cool down and recover.

    When you’re feeling stressed, techniques like box breathing, deep belly breathing, and 4–7–8 breathing can be especially helpful as they’re designed to quickly calm your body and mind.

    Box breathing uses equal counts of inhale, hold, exhale, and pause, which creates a steady rhythm that helps quiet anxious thoughts.

    Deep belly breathing slows your breath and encourages your muscles to relax.

    The 4-7-8 technique calms the nervous system in order to calm the stress.

    Closing the Skills Gap for Autistic Employees

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (489 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Additudemag

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the unemployment rate for workers with autism is staggering.
    • It has been revealed that in Australia, the unemployment rate for neurodivergent adults hovers around 34%, nearly eight times the national average.
    • ASA was established in 2020 to increase workforce participation among young neurodivergent adults by training them in big data for the geospatial and digital engineering fields, then placing them in corporate and government sectors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the unemployment rate for workers with autism is staggering. One Australian manufacturer is aiming to change that.

    It has been revealed that in Australia, the unemployment rate for neurodivergent adults hovers around 34%, nearly eight times the national average. Clearly, there is a stigma around hiring neurodivergent people and it stems from a fear of the unknown. One not-for-profit manufacturer, Australian Spatial Analytics (ASA), is working to fix that.

    ASA was established in 2020 to increase workforce participation among young neurodivergent adults by training them in big data for the geospatial and digital engineering fields, then placing them in corporate and government sectors. At ASA, we leverage these employees’ cognitive strengths — attention to detail, pattern recognition, laser-sharp focus, and innovative problem-solving skills, all of which are invaluable in these fields.

    About 80% of ASA’s staff identify as neurodivergent, which includes ADHD, autism, dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dyspraxia. ASA’s recruitment process goes beyond conventional practices; it assesses potential candidates based on transferable skills, hobbies, and interests, rather than relying on formal qualifications or previous experience. Many of the new data analysts we have successfully placed in jobs are in paid positions for the first time.

    [Read: We’re Hiring – ADHD-Friendly Careers].

    Industry observers note that yet the analysts’ value to their employers is without questions. Executives have praised the ASA-trained analysts who have joined their companies, citing their work ethic, dedication, and problem-solving skills.

    It has been revealed that during the job-seeking process, ASA provides candidates with sample interview questions 48 hours in advance to help minimize anxiety. Once hired, employees receive comprehensive and paid on-the-job training that includes soft skills like communication and self-advocacy coaching.

    [Read: Nail Your Job Interview – 3 Strategies for Neurodivergent Applicants].

    It has been revealed that based on our experience, creating a supportive and productive environment requires only minor accommodations. Flexible start and finish times, predictable routines, the option for hybrid work to reduce commuting stress, adjustable lighting, noise-canceling headphones, and direct communication make a profound difference, not only for neurodivergent people, but for everyone in the workplace.

    To help change paradigms, ASA offers a Neurodiversity in the Workplace Training Program for other organizations. It covers neurodiversity awareness, plus effective strategies for communication, managing anxiety in the work environment, leading neurodiverse teams, and promoting neurodivergent inclusion.

    Ultimately, our goal is to put ourselves out of business.

    Karly Ischenko is a Human Resources Business Partner at Australian Spatial Analytics.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • Roughly half of adults in treatment for eating disorders display symptoms of ADHD, though few are diagnosed, according to a newly introduced cross-sectional study published in Journal of Eating Disorders.1.
    • The study, conducted at Esquirol Hospital in Limoges, France, included 120 participants, 95.8% of whom were female.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    More than 50% of people receiving treatment for eating disorders, especially bulimia and binge-eating, may have ADHD, though few are diagnosed, according to a new study.

    Roughly half of adults in treatment for eating disorders display symptoms of ADHD, though few are diagnosed, according to a newly introduced cross-sectional study published in Journal of Eating Disorders.1.

    The study, conducted at Esquirol Hospital in Limoges, France, included 120 participants, 95.8% of whom were female. Using the ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS v1.1), researchers screened participants for ADHD, then followed up to confirm the screening with the Diagnostic Interview for ADHD (DIVA 2.0). More than half (61) of the participants met criteria for ADHD, according to these measures, though only two had received a prior diagnosis. Bulimia nervosa and binge-eating disorder were more strongly associated with ADHD than was anorexia nervosa.

    Participants who revealed symptoms of ADHD also had more psychiatric comorbidities and higher rates of impulsivity, body dissatisfaction, and smoking and alcohol use. Personality assessments revealed that participants with ADHD symptoms showed greater dependence on rewards, while those who did not exhibited higher rates of self-regulation.

    “These findings support ADHD screening and integrated treatments targeting impulsivity and attentional dysregulation,” wrote the study’s authors.

    In “ADHD and Eating Disorders: Research, Diagnosis & Treatment Guidelines,” Roberto Olivardia, Ph.D., explores the myriad biological and genetic factors that may predispose individuals with ADHD to eating disorders. They include:.

    Further research is needed to understand all possible mechanisms, as well as the benefit of ADHD treatment on eating disorder recovery.

    In an ADDitude guest blog post titled, “Dopamine, Not Discipline: The ADHD–Eating Disorder Link I Was Missing,” Penelope Mazzetti offers these insights: “My ‘out-of-control eating’ wasn’t an concern of willpower; it was partly sensory-seeking behavior, a well-documented ADHD trait. As ADHD brains like mine are chronically low in dopamine, we are wired to seek stimulation, and food just happens to be fast, legal, and always available.”.

    1Bonilla, A., Torelli, S., Virevialle, AL. et al. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in adults with eating disorders: prevalence, clinical correlates, and personality profiles. J Eat Disord (2026). https://doi.org/10.1186/s40337-026-01793-6.

    #114964. Why Kids with ADHD Get Stuck in the Screen-Time Loop. And How to Break It.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1053 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Additudemag ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Kids with ADHD Get Stuck in the Screen-Time Loop. And How to Break It.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Additudemag

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The adolescent prefrontal cortex is no match for addictive-by-design apps and games.
    • In a recent development, screen addiction is not the problem.
    • Industry observers note that once you understand that distinction, you can stop fighting the wrong battle and start winning the right one.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The adolescent prefrontal cortex is no match for addictive-by-design apps and games. Learn why ADHD brains get hooked on these “other stimulants,” and how to protect them.

    In a recent development, screen addiction is not the problem. Your child is not hooked on their phone, but rather the endless loop of novelty, stimulation, and unpredictable rewards streaming through it. It’s the dopamine; not the device.

    Industry observers note that once you understand that distinction, you can stop fighting the wrong battle and start winning the right one. Here’s the central point: Phones and video games weren’t as addictive before they got connected to the Internet. A standalone game that you can beat has an ending. A connected game like Fortnite, Roblox, or Minecraft never ends.

    For a kid with ADHD, whose brain runs on a dopamine deficit, the Internet is impossible to resist – by design. We hand the most addictive delivery system ever built to the most vulnerable brains, and then ask them to show self-control. That’s not a fair fight.

    Adolescents and teens with ADHD find screens irresistible, and it’s no wonder why. The ADHD brain is dopamine-deficient, and screens deliver dopamine instantly, reliably, and without effort. Almost everything else in life – school, sports, chores, homework – delivers dopamine slowly, inconsistently, and with lots of effort. The brain always chooses the path of least resistance to its dopamine.

    This isn’t a character flaw or a discipline problem. It’s neurology. The dopamine hit from a connected screen is more powerful and more reinforcing for an ADHD brain than it is for a neurotypical one because the ADHD brain is always hunting for dopamine.

    [Download: Managing and Safeguarding Your Child’s Screen Time].

    A 2023 meta-analysis of more than 81,000 children found that two or more hours a day of screen time were associated with significantly elevated ADHD risk compared with less than two hours.1 Large longitudinal data from a separate study, which tracked more than 10,000 kids for two years, found that more screen time predicted increased ADHD – and that changes in brain structure helped explain the link.2.

    Imaging research has tied greater screen time to altered development in the orbitofrontal cortex, lateral prefrontal cortex, and anterior cingulate cortex – the regions that govern attention, cognitive control, and reward.

    It has been revealed that back in the 1950s, the psychologist B.F. Skinner discovered something the entire tech industry would later weaponize: The most powerful way to drive a behavior isn’t to reward it every time, but to reward it unpredictably. It’s called a variable-ratio reinforcement schedule, and it’s the most addictive reward pattern known to behavioral science.

    It is why slot machines are built as they are. You pull the lever, and you might get nothing, or you might hit the jackpot. Not knowing is what keeps you pulling.

    [Read: How Can I Help My Teen Better Manage Screen Time?].

    Industry observers note that the same mechanism is now built into the games and apps your child uses every day. The loot box that might contain something rare. The next Roblox round that might go better. The Snapchat notification that might be from someone who matters. The Fortnite match that might end in a Victory Royale. The brain releases dopamine in anticipation of the reward, not when it arrives. This is why your child can’t stop.

    Sources indicate that but disconnect the device, and the compulsion largely collapses: the variable rewards stop, the social pressure disappears, and the relentless loop finally ends. You don’t have to eliminate every screen, but you must control the connection.

    According to recent reports, the brain’s prefrontal cortex (the executive function center) isn’t fully developed until around age 25, and perhaps later in an individual with ADHD. Every year you delay access to the Internet is another year of maturity for your child’s executive function system before it’s asked to regulate the most dysregulating product ever made.

    Sources indicate that this is why a growing chorus of researchers is now urging parents to delay smartphones until at least high school (around age 14) and social media until at least age 16. The logic is simple: Let the most vulnerable period of brain development happen before your child can access the loop.

    In a recent development, here’s the empowering part: You control the devices, the accounts, the passwords, the router, and the timing of introduction. The strategy below is about exerting that control through environmental design – not nagging, not negotiating, not hoping a dysregulated brain suddenly regulates itself.

    STEP 1: Make a pact. Counter the “I’m the only one without a phone” argument by encouraging three or four other families to agree to delay access together. Ask the parents of your child’s friends to make the pact. It’s easier to hold the line together than alone.

    STEP 2: Stop competing with the screen. Control access to the dopamine source through environmental design, not willpower. Screens go in a central location after a certain hour. Devices charge outside bedrooms, every night, no exceptions.

    Industry observers note that STEP 3: Build “earn-access” systems. Screens become available only after the non-negotiables are done. Homework must be completed, then Xbox. Follow the simple, consistent rules every single day. The structure does the work so you don’t have to matter the reminder.

    Michael McLeod is the founder of GrowNOW ADHD and the author of The Executive Function Playbook.

    How to love yourself: 7 steps to learn self-love

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3394 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that clinically reviewed by Dr.
    • In a recent development, learning how to love yourself can feel unfamiliar—especially if your inner voice leans more critical than kind.
    • If you’ve ever asked yourself, “How do I love myself?” or wondered what the actual meaning of self-love is, you’re not alone.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, CDCES, MBA.

    In a recent development, learning how to love yourself can feel unfamiliar—especially if your inner voice leans more critical than kind. But here’s the truth: self-love isn’t something you’re born knowing how to do. It’s something you learn. And like any meaningful practice, it takes time, intention, and a lot of patience.

    If you’ve ever asked yourself, “How do I love myself?” or wondered what the actual meaning of self-love is, you’re not alone. Many of us were never taught how to speak to ourselves with compassion, how to set boundaries that honor our needs, or how to practice everyday self-respect. That’s where this guide comes in—because it’s never too late to build a more loving relationship with yourself.

    In a recent development, developing self-love doesn’t mean you’re selfish or self-centered. It means learning to treat yourself the way you’d treat someone you care deeply about—with gentleness, understanding, and care. Whether you’re struggling with self-worth, navigating difficult emotions, or simply trying to reconnect with the real you, these seven steps offer a foundation for how to practice self-love in real, actionable ways.

    From building self-awareness and setting healthy boundaries to practicing forgiveness and celebrating your wins, this guide is here to support your growth. Start small, stay consistent, and trust that loving yourself is not only possible—it’s one of the most empowering things you’ll ever do.

    In a recent development, self-love is exactly how it sounds—it’s a love for yourself and having an interest in your own well-being and happiness. Loving yourself doesn’t mean being self-centered or selfish. It’s about forming a caring relationship with yourself, like getting to know a good friend.

    The idea of loving yourself isn’t just a ‘feel-good’ concept—it’s essential for mental health. Research shows that self-compassion is linked to lower stress, reduced anxiety, and even improved physical health. People who actively practice self-love tend to set better boundaries, build stronger relationships, and experience less burnout.

    It has been revealed that self-love is important because the relationship you have with yourself sets the tone for how you deal with every aspect of life: your bonds with others, the way you handle challenges, and how you celebrate joys. When you’re kind and understanding toward yourself, you’re better equipped to navigate life’s ups and downs.

    Sources indicate that but how do you start loving yourself? Where do you even begin? Self-love starts with understanding where you stand right now. Take a look at your current feelings toward your mental health, motivation, and overall well-being. Are you harsh with yourself when things don’t go as planned? Do you forget to celebrate your wins, especially the small ones? These little check-ins can pave the path to walking toward self-love.

    According to recent reports, loving yourself isn’t a switch you turn on or off. It’s a practice that takes time, commitment, and, well, practice, to cultivate. For many of us, the idea of loving ourselves feels out of reach. That’s why it’s often helpful to break the concept of self-love down into its distinctive elements — including self-trust, self-compassion, and self-awareness.

    In a recent development, this can make it easier to start developing a self-love practice that feels achievable and manageable. So instead of viewing self-love as something you have to win at, try practicing these seven steps.

    Self-awareness: Understand your feelings, thoughts, and behaviors.

    Self-expression: Be true to who you are in all areas of life.

    Self-care: Take care of your body and mind.

    Self-trust: Believe in your ability to handle life’s ups and downs.

    Self-compassion: Be kind to yourself, especially when times are tough.

    Self-respect: Honor your worth by setting healthy boundaries.

    Self-acceptance: Embrace who you are, including the parts you don’t find perfect. Remember what we noted about perfection?

    Sometimes practicing self-love means taking action or establishing boundaries to protect your mental health. Here are a few IRL examples of how you can practice self-love today.

    Prioritize rest to recharge: Imagine you’ve had a long week, and instead of squeezing in one more task, you decide to turn off your devices and enjoy a full night’s sleep. Studies have shown that adequate rest improves mood, cognitive function, and emotional resilience​. By honoring your body’s need for recovery, you demonstrate that you value your well-being above productivity.

    Say no to unhealthy relationships: Picture being invited to a gathering where you know that certain individuals drain your energy. Choosing to decline isn't selfish; it’s self-preservation. Healthy boundaries are key to having self-respect and healthy relationships. Saying no clears space for connections that truly nourish you​.

    Practice forgiveness for yourself: Maybe you’ve made a mistake at work and feel embarrassed. Instead of spiraling into self-criticism, try acknowledging the error, learning from it, and moving on. Self-compassion may help reduce anxiety and create more resilience, helping you recover more effectively from setbacks​. Mistakes are normal, and it’s all about “failing up”.

    Industry observers note that create moments of mindfulness amid the chaos: Let’s say your day is hectic, and stress feels overwhelming. This is the moment to pause for a brief grounding exercise (here’s one of our favorites). Maybe you focus on your breath or tune into your surroundings. These types of practice not only calm your nervous system but also remind you of your ability to care for yourself even in small, meaningful ways​.

    Treat yourself with the same kindness you show others: When you reflect on a recent accomplishment—big or small—you choose to celebrate it instead of brushing it off. There are huge benefits to recognizing your personal achievements. Giving yourself a pat on the back may help boost self-esteem and even long-term happiness​.

    According to recent reports, self-love can feel unfamiliar and challenging to some of us, particularly if we’ve got into a habit of being hard on ourselves. The steps above can help break down the idea of self-love into more manageable elements.

    Sources indicate that but what practical things can we do to cultivate practices like self-awareness and self-trust? We got you. For each of the self-love steps, we’re sharing tools, techniques and exercises you can use to help get you closer to loving yourself.

    Building self-awareness helps cultivate self-love by giving you further insight into what makes you who you are on an emotional level. Begin by tuning into your thoughts and feelings.

    What makes you feel happy, sad, or excited? Then, take it a step further. What makes you feel overwhelmed, overjoyed, or anxious? Knowing yourself is the first step to loving yourself.

    Practice mindfulness: Try mindfulness practices to stay present and understand your thoughts and feelings better.

    Educate yourself: Empower yourself through education by reading books, attending workshops, or engaging in discussions that promote self-awareness, self-compassion, and self-love.

    Schedule regular self-check-ins: Reflect on your feelings, goals, and progress. Write them down, and revisit them often.

    Tune into yourself through meditation: Spend some quiet time meditating to help declutter your mind and tap into your desires.

    Let go of what no longer serves you: Let go of old habits or relationships that no longer contribute to your growth or happiness. We know this practice can be difficult, but removing what no longer brings you joy makes space for the good to come in.

    💙 If you want to learn to relate to your thoughts in a healthier way, press play on Shift Your Perspective with Jay Shetty.

    It has been revealed that loving yourself also means giving yourself permission to express your thoughts and feelings both inwardly and outwardly. Express yourself honestly in your day-to-day life. Be true to who you are, whether you’re simply chatting with friends or making substantial decisions at work.

    Engage in creative expression: Whether it's drawing, writing, or any other form of creative expression, allowing your creativity to flow freely can become an act of self-love.

    Industry observers note that discover new hobbies: Explore new activities that bring you joy and allow you to express yourself. Have you always wanted to try your hand at a group sport or acting? Now’s the time to try.

    It has been revealed that journaling: Write down your thoughts, feelings, and experiences daily, and don’t hold back. Expressing yourself through writing can be cathartic and a helpful step in falling back in love with who you are.

    According to recent reports, spend quality time with yourself: Enjoy your own tech giant by doing things that make you happy. There’s a difference between doing something alone and feeling lonely. Embracing solo time and solo outings to the movies, dinner, or even a cooking class can be empowering, and, believe it or not, ridiculously fun!

    💙 Journaling can be a great way to process feelings and encourage self-love. Check out our five Calm Journals plus our Feelings Wheel to get you started.

    It has been revealed that caring for your body and mind plays a major role in cultivating self-love. Simple acts like mindful eating, exercise, and making time to relax can make a significant difference in your overall well-being.

    Take breaks when you need them: Remember to rest — even a micro-break can refresh and rejuvenate you. Want to amp up your rest break a notch? Take it outside. Being in nature can naturally calm and refresh your mind and body.

    Practice relaxation: Use techniques like deep breathing or yoga to relax your body and focus on your breath.

    Nourish your body: Fuel your body with nourishing food that makes you feel good.

    Prioritize sleep: Ensure you get enough good-quality sleep—it’s crucial for your well-being.

    Recent findings suggest that connect with your body through movement: Move your body in a way that feels good for you. It could be dancing in your apartment to your favorite album, walking outside, or stretching from the comfort of your bed.

    Ask for support when you need it: Reach out for help when you need it. Asking for support is a sign of strength.

    💙 Move your body with some Mindful Movement thanks to the Daily Move.

    Sources indicate that it’s hard to love yourself if you don’t trust yourself. Embracing self-trust is about understanding that you have the ability to make the correct decisions for your life. Even when things don’t go as planned, believing that you can learn and grow from the experience is an important step in building self-trust.

    Set realistic expectations: Set achievable goals to build your sense of accomplishment and reinforce the belief you have in yourself to overcome.

    Igor Nora builds the Parniera brand identity from silk and sculpted gold, with a bespoke typeface and a silk moth mark in pale yellow.

    According to recent reports, the idea is a collision the project calls Sculpted Duality. On one side, fine silk in fluid motion, pale yellow, soft and light. On the other, solid sculpted gold forms with architectural weight. The identity holds both at once: garments described as vulnerability and armor, built for a woman who commands the room with quiet power. Nothing shouts. The yellow field does the talking, and the black line work sits on it with total control.

    Sources indicate that the wordmark is a bespoke typeface drawn for the house. Thin, delicate strokes carry the lightness, while high contrast serifs give the letters their structure. The detail that holds it together is the ligatures: internal connective strokes, clearest in the N, I, E and R, link the characters the way woven silk holds a thread, so the name reads as one continuous piece. A construction frame shows the letters PA on black, with guide bars and notes on the straight serifs and the joins between letters.

    Industry observers note that the moth mark works the same way. It is built from four overlapping geometric forms, a line drawing of the Bombyx mori silk moth, the living link between the Persian name Parnia, a canvas of fine silk, and the sculpted gold the house stands for.

    It has been revealed that the system stays physical wherever it lands. The moth mark sits alone on a pale yellow tile, then repeats as a woven petal pattern in yellow, gold and tan. The brand book opens in a black ring binder: a yellow page carries the wordmark embossed into the paper, facing a white page headed "Essence of allure." The same yellow carries the shopping bag, the wordmark pressed into the paper along the bottom edge, with black ribbon handles.

    At street level the system scales up without changing its voice. A tall yellow banner hangs on a red brick building beside a panel with the moth mark, and the closing collage pulls the whole world together: moth tile, beaded gown detail, patterned envelope, shopping bag, the wordmark on yellow, and the line "Presence without the noise." It is a quiet luxury, stated once and left alone.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Here’s how to stir up stronger connections, repair misunderstandings, and nurture relationships.

    Time, similarities, vibes, and luck – these are the four core ingredients of friendship. Blended into the mix for adults with ADHD are anxiety, rejection sensitive dysphoria (RSD), impulsivity, and social acuity.

    The friendship recipe varies by person and circumstance, but the following strategies almost always help.

    The challenge: Attention regulation problems may cause you to mentally drift, dominate conversations, or impulsively interrupt.

    [Get This Free Download: The ADHD Friendship Guide for Adults].

    You’re tracking multiple stimuli simultaneously – body language, tone, word choice, environmental distractions – while managing your own impulses. This requires significantly more energy than most people realize and can result in unintentional social withdrawal.

    Use this gauge to monitor your energy levels throughout a social interaction: 10 = Fully charged 4 = Running low; time to recharge 0 = Want to hide under the covers.

    You may fear that recharging will damage your relationships, but taking time to rest is the smart choice that allows you to show up as your best self in your relationships.

    The dopamine thrill of a newly introduced friendship can cause us to text too frequently, share too much too soon, or pressure still-developing friendships. Avoid coming on too strong.

    [Read: ADHD and the Social Processing Gap].

    Sometimes the challenge isn’t making friends but discerning whether a particular person deserves space in your life.

    People pleasing, over-apologizing, overthinking, and shame spirals are signs of RSD.

    Amy Kempe, LPC, is the owner of Authentic Life Therapy in Philadelphia.

    #114959. How to lower your heart rate quickly (and keep it healthy)
